item.title: US Army detonates toxic explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Army detonated a massive cache of toxic explosives stored in a tiny Iowa farming town on Wednesday, saying the materials were too unstable to move to a safer area and warning residents to shelter from the blast and a potential cloud of lead dust. Officials said the 68 drums of lead azide — the entire U.S. stockpile of the degraded material — were at risk of spontaneous explosion, requiring their destruction at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, where they had been stored for more than 15 years. Measures were put in place to curb potential contamination from the destruction of the nearly five tons of explosive material, but the Army encouraged residents of Middletown, Iowa and other nearby areas to leave prior to the blast "out of an abundance of caution." Locals taped up windows to guard against flying glass and were urged to stay indoors to avoid possible toxic dust. item.title: US proposes tariffs over excess production, retains 15% cap for Korea, Japan, EU
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday fired a new tariff salvo on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in U.S. midterm elections. His administration proposed new headline tariff rates of 20 percent to 40 percent, but said duties would be capped at lower levels agreed under trade deals that have already been concluded or remain under negotiation. Separately, the United States Trade Representative proposed a new 10 percent tariff on imports of Brazil's finished Embraer commercial aircraft, and to raise duties on imports of Brazilian sugar that exceed quotas as part of an effort to push Brasilia to rectify alleged unfair trade practices. The products were previously exempted from Trump's 25 percent tariffs on Brazilian goods that were imposed in July. A U.S. official said that despite negotiations, there were "substantial differences" over the allegations. Under the main "Section 301" probe into excess industrial capacity, China would face the highest capped

item.title: From 6 days to 5: Busan subway cleaners finally find time for life beyond work
item.description: “Back then, there were no machines. You had to wring it out by hand. You step on this bar with your foot, grab the two strands of the mop and twist them tightly with your rubber-gloved hands.” Han Kyung-sun, 66, demonstrated how to wring out a mop, springing to her feet as she explained the evolution of cleaning equipment at Minam Station on Busan Metro Line 3 on Nov. 10. Wearing red rubber gloves, she gripped the mop strands and twisted them, sending dirty water dripping to the floor. Han is a 16-year veteran cleaner employed by Busan Transportation Operation & Service. She is currently responsible for the station's restrooms, escalators, platform screens and station office. When she first started cleaning, she had to wring out heavy, water-soaked mops with both hands. Later, a foot-operated mop wringer, nicknamed “squeezer,” made the work easier. This year, the introduction of wet vacuums further reduced her workload. Han, who used to carry buckets, mops and a wringer, now heads into the station with just a vacuum cleaner and a damp mop. item.title: Mathmatician-turned-Buddhist monk leans into inner cultivation for AI era
item.description: “Inner cultivation to manage alienation and depression will become increasingly important in the age of artificial intelligence (AI). We need ‘metacognition’ — the ability to objectively observe our own mental state — to regulate and overcome our emotions.” Ven. Ilmuk, a 61-year-old Buddhist monk who has practiced meditation in Korea and abroad for 30 years and taught meditation, has published his first book in five years, "Buddha’s Breathing Meditation" (Bulkwang Publishing). Based on the early Buddhist scripture "Anapanasati Sutta" (Mindfulness of Breathing), the book offers a detailed guide to the principles and practice of breathing meditation. It covers everything from the basic steps of observing one’s breath to obstacles that hinder meditation and ways to overcome them, as well as the process of cultivating concentration and wisdom to end suffering. The book presents breathing meditation as a path that leads beyond mental tranquility to liberation. item.title: Inflation remains uncomfortably high despite retreat in gas prices as challenges mount for the Fed
item.description: WASHINGTON — A key inflation gauge remained high last month even as gas prices cooled in a sign that elevated costs remain a challenge for the Federal Reserve and elected officials in Washington. The Commerce Department said Wednesday that consumer prices rose 3.8 percent in October from a year earlier, up from 3.6 percent in September. On a monthly basis, consumer prices climbed 0.3 percent from September to October, down from a 0.6 percent increase the previous month. The stubbornly elevated price figures come as the economy is expanding at a healthy pace, driven by strong consumer spending and surging business investment as large tech firms splurge on building out AI infrastructure. Consumer spending has been resilient even as persistent inflation raises the costs of many necessities and has soured most Americans on the economy. Yet much of the spending is driven by upper-income households, and there are signs poorer Americans are relying more on credit to sustain their spending. item.title: US finds no evidence China directed executive to spy on Nvidia CEO, WSJ reports
item.description: U.S. officials found no evidence that tech executive Alice Huang was directed by Beijing to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with a classified briefing. The briefing comes after U.S. President Donald Trump cleared the way for Jensen Huang's reinstatement earlier this week, assuring Nvidia that its CEO posed no national-security threat. The controversy began with concerns over Alice Huang's alleged Chinese intelligence links and whether her relationship with Jensen Huang affected suspected diversions of Nvidia chips to China. Officials from the CIA, FBI, Office of the Director of National Intelligence and National Security Agency briefed staff from congressional intelligence committees and chamber leaders, the Journal reported. The officials said Alice Huang contacted China's spy agency during the affair but found no indication that she provided significant intelligence, the Journal reported. item.title: US Justice Dept did not open probe into Huang before reinstatement, sources say
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Justice Department did not conduct a formal investigation into Jensen Huang before U.S. President Donald Trump pushed for his return as Nvidia chief executive this week, despite active probes into the chipmaker's customers and allegations he conducted an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence, according to three people familiar with the matter. Instead, Attorney General Todd Blanche concluded that there was no evidence the tech titan had broken any laws based on the Justice Department's ongoing investigations into two Nvidia clients, Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, which are suspected of smuggling advanced microchips to China, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity. That determination, which is subject to change as the probes continue, was crucial to Blanche's decision to tell Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the weekend that he possessed no evidence that Huang posed a risk to national security, said two of the people. Jensen Huang's reinstatement has angered members of Congress — both Republicans and Democrats

item.title: Iran says Israel trying to deceive US into war with chemical weapons claim
item.description: TEHRAN — Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Israel was trying to drag the United States into another war after an Israeli minister alleged Tehran is building chemical weapons. "This warmonger shamelessly accuses Iran... of developing and concealing such heinous weapons in pharmaceutical factories. The objective is audacious: to deceive the U.S. into fighting yet another war on its behalf," he wrote in a statement posted on X. Israel has for years accused Iran of trying to acquire nuclear weapons, but Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz on Tuesday alleged Tehran is building chemical weapons and vowed to stop the Islamic republic from obtaining them. "Iran is in the process of developing chemical weapons but has not yet reached the capability to attack Israel with them," said Katz in a statement published by his Likud party on Telegram. "We must not allow this to proceed." But a key ally of Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said Wednesday there was no need to attack Iran immediately and questioned the caretaker government's intentions. Avigdor Liberm

item.title: Nasdaq sinks about 4% as AI rout, fresh Trump tariffs spook Wall St
item.description: The main U.S. indexes fell on Wednesday, with the Nasdaq plunging about 4 percent, as a deepening selloff in AI-related stocks and new U.S. tariff proposals hit sentiment amid mounting doubt over whether the debt-fueled AI boom can deliver sufficient returns. Wall Street has been roiled this month, with fears of increased regulatory scrutiny of the AI sector following the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections adding to the pressure. "The fundamental support for a year-end rally simply isn't there," Chris Brigati, chief investment officer at SWBC, said in a note. "The AI-inspired rally continues to run out of steam, and without evidence that massive capex spending will deliver the profit and revenue goals the market expects, there is little incentive for a rebound." Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO after his removal earlier this month provided a temporary reprieve at the start of the week. Broader concerns lingered, however, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq and the S&P 500 remained on track for their worst November since 2008. Chipmakers led the declines, with Nvidia falling 8.7 percent an

item.title: Gold falls 3% to more than one-year low after data shows US inflation rose further
item.description: Gold fell more than 3 percent to its lowest level in more than a year after strong U.S. inflation data failed to assuage concerns surrounding the Federal Reserve's rate-hike path. Spot gold was down 3 percent to $3,445.89 per ounce by 11:13 a.m. ET (1613 GMT), hitting its lowest level since August 2025. The metal fell below the key $3,500 level for the first time since September 2025. U.S. gold futures for December delivery dropped 3.3 percent to $3,445.10. U.S. inflation rose further in October, with the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index rising 0.3 percent after an unrevised 0.5 percent gain in September, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said on Wednesday. "With inflationary pressures remaining significantly above the Fed target, the likelihood continues that the Fed will raise interest rates moving forward, which adds pressure to gold," David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures, said. "That's been one of the main themes that remains a headwind for the gold market, and today's PCE data did nothing to allay those concerns." Elevated rates

item.title: N. Korea expels Swiss diplomat over sanctions weeks after office reopening
item.description: North Korea has expelled the head of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang and ordered the envoy to leave within 48 hours, its foreign ministry said on Wednesday, in a spat over sanctions less than a month after Bern reopened the office. The ministry said the move was in response to the Swiss decision to put sanctions on North Korea's Songdowon International Children's Camp, calling it an overtly hostile act in a statement carried by the state-run Korean Central News Agency. Pyongyang's Foreign Ministry summoned the head of the diplomatic office, Sylvain Astier, and handed him a memorandum urging him to close the office, the news agency said. "The Foreign Ministry of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea declared the head of the Swiss Diplomatic Office in the DPRK persona non grata and urged him to leave the country within 48 hours," it said, using the country's official name. "Any act of violating the sovereign rights of the DPRK and the interests of its citizens can never be welcomed by us." item.title: 'Hope' wins top Blue Dragon award; Sul, Jeon take acting honors for 'Possible Love'
item.description: Director Na Hong-jin's sci-fi thriller "Hope" won best picture at the 47th Blue Dragon Film Awards on Wednesday, while Lee Chang-dong's "Possible Love" emerged as the night's biggest winner with four awards, including both top acting honors. "Hope," which competed at this year's Cannes Film Festival, entered the ceremony at KBS Hall in Seoul with a leading 10 nominations and also won the cinematography and lighting award. Accepting the best picture trophy, Na drew laughter from the audience by joking that he should have won the award at Cannes. "They should have given me this at Cannes. Why here instead?" he said. Na then credited the cast and crew, describing the experience of making the film as one of the happiest and most memorable times of his life. Meanwhile, Lee's "Possible Love," which won the Grand Jury Prize at this year's Venice International Film Festival, dominated the acting categories. Sul Kyung-gu and Jeon Do-yeon, who play a married couple in the drama exploring class divisions, won best actor and best actress, respectively. Their co-star Cho Yeo-jeong took home best suppor

item.title: Anthropic's slide tests Wall Street's lofty bets on future AI profits
item.description: Anthropic's slide below its initial public offering price has sharpened investor scrutiny of lofty technology valuations, as markets increasingly question whether even the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom can generate enough profit to justify their price tags. Shares of the Claude developer were trading around $80.50, well below their $83 offer price and nearly 30 percent below their opening price on November 19. The swift reversal highlights growing unease over how much investors are willing to pay for future growth, even as earnings prospects improve for many companies benefiting from artificial intelligence. Of the 86 Nasdaq-100 companies with positive earnings multiples and available earnings revision data, 60 saw their forward 12-month earnings forecasts rise over the past three months, a Reuters analysis of LSEG data showed. Yet, shares in 37 of those companies declined over the same period. item.title: FM Cho asks Omani counterpart to keep backing Cheonghae unit
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met his Omani counterpart, Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi, on Wednesday and asked Oman to keep backing the Cheonghae naval unit, which operates in waters off the Gulf state, the ministry said. Cho thanked Oman, a key port of call for the unit, for helping it run its missions smoothly. Al Busaidi, for his part, vowed to continue that support, according to the ministry. Earlier in the day, the defense committee of Korea's National Assembly approved a revised motion to extend the unit's operational zone from the Gulf of Aden to the open sea south of Oman. The motion also widens its role in securing safe maritime passage. Cho stressed that Oman is one of Korea's key energy partners and called on the Gulf country to support Korean businesses working in its renewable energy and energy infrastructure sectors. Al Busaidi's trip marked the first visit by an Omani foreign minister since July 2000.

item.title: 6 dead, 20 believed trapped after flood hits unauthorized gold mine in Indonesia
item.description: JAKARTA, Indonesia — Rescuers in Indonesia recovered three more bodies from an unauthorized gold mine Wednesday and searched for 20 other miners believed trapped inside by flooding, raising the confirmed number of deaths to six. The miners were digging for grains of gold late Monday when heavy rain caused the nearby Ciseureuh River to overflow into a mine shaft in the Bogor regency of West Java province. The shaft, estimated to be about 100 meters deep, is located in a mountainous area south of the capital, Jakarta. Eleven miners escaped from one section of the excavation before floodwaters filled the shaft, West Java police spokesperson Hendra Rochmawan said. Local miners and residents initially tried to pump water from the site themselves before the situation became unmanageable. Authorities were not immediately notified because the miners were operating illegally, officials said. “The problem was that nobody reported it and nobody wanted to report it because the activity was illegal,” said Muhammad Adam Hamdani, head of emergency and logistics at the Bogor disaster mitigation age

item.title: UN warns of growing risk of atrocities by Israel against Palestinians
item.description: GENEVA, Switzerland — The United Nations warned Wednesday of a growing risk of atrocity crimes being committed by Israel against the Palestinians, and urged all states to take immediate preventative action. U.N. rights chief Volker Turk said ongoing Israeli attacks, policies and violations against Palestinians indicated a "widening risk of further atrocity crimes" in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. "Israeli government representatives at highest levels have time and again spelled out policies of annexation, ethnic cleansing and collective punishment in the West Bank," he said in a statement. "Across society, the incitement to hatred and to perpetration of violations amounting to atrocity crimes — war crimes, crimes against humanity and even genocide — has been appalling." Turk said his office had repeatedly warned about the risk of Israel's actions in Gaza posing a "real threat to the continued existence" of the Palestinians as a group. item.title: Hanwha Ocean loses preferred bidder status for Thai frigate project
item.description: Hanwha Ocean has lost its preferred bidder status for a next-generation Thai frigate project after the Royal Thai Navy canceled the procurement process, sending the Korean shipbuilder’s entry into the Thai naval market back to square one, the company said Wednesday. “Hanwha Ocean was selected as the preferred bidder for the frigate project ordered by the Royal Thai Navy on Sept. 8, but lost its preferred bidder status following the Royal Thai Navy’s announcement, Wednesday, canceling the procurement process,” Hanwha Ocean said in a regulatory filing. The Royal Thai Navy selected Hanwha Ocean as its preferred bidder in September, beating defense companies from Spain, Singapore and Turkey. The project involved building one frigate and providing integrated logistics support, with the proposed contract valued at around 680 billion won ($505 million). item.title: Son Suk-ku on 'The Blue Road,' his career's second chapter
item.description: Korean actor Son Suk-ku has opened up about the deep psychological and physical preparation behind his latest role in the Netflix mystery thriller series "The Blue Road," a gripping cross-border crime drama featuring an unprecedented investigative partnership between top representative actors from Korea and Japan. Following two detectives investigating a string of gruesome international murders marked by twisted corpses and cryptic messages, the series stars Son as Kim Seok, a sharp-witted and relentless detective with the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency, who teams up with a Japanese counterpart to crack the case. item.title: President reaffirms Cheonghae unit will widen role, but stay out of war
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday reaffirmed that Korea's Cheonghae naval unit will take on a wider role in securing safe maritime passage, but will not intervene in any war. His remarks followed a vote earlier in the day by the National Assembly's defense committee approving a revised motion to widen the unit's operational zone. The unit would move from the waters off Somalia to the Arabian Sea south of Oman, about 650 kilometers from the Strait of Hormuz. "As I said in September, the dispatch of the unit will neither involve us in a war nor intervene in one," Lee wrote on his X account. "We will use this extension of the unit's mission period to broaden its role and strengthen its combat capabilities," he said. On the specifics, he said, "We will add maritime patrol aircraft and mine-clearing support to the destroyer's existing role and extend its operation area from the Gulf of Aden to the open sea south of Oman." item.title: Additional personal info leaked from Bithumb in cyberattacks
item.description: More personal information than initially reported had been leaked from Bithumb in a recent cyberattack, the cryptocurrency exchange said Wednesday. Bithumb reported a data breach late last month affecting some 7,100 customers and employees, but the exchange said more personal information has been compromised. The leaked personal information includes names, phone numbers, passport numbers and account numbers. Financial firms, such as Mirae Asset Securities and Daishin Securities, have suffered a series of cyberattacks.

item.title: Hahm Sung-deuk named acting president of Kyonggi University
item.description: Kyonggi University has appointed Hahm Sung-deuk, a political science professor and vice president of its Seoul campus, as acting president, the university said Monday. The appointment followed the succession order stipulated in the university's bylaws and organizational regulations, according to the university. The position has been vacant since late July, when Ko Gi-bok was removed from office over allegations of sexual assault involving a former student. Hahm received his doctorate in political economy from Carnegie Mellon University in the United States. He previously taught at Georgetown University and Korea University before joining Kyonggi University in 2021 as dean of its Graduate School of Political Studies. As acting president, he will oversee the university's academic and administrative affairs until a new president is appointed. The timeline for selecting a permanent president has yet to be determined. item.title: Delta sides with Korean Air leadership in Hanjin KAL ownership battle
item.description: Delta Air Lines has dealt a setback to Hoban Group's push for control of Hanjin KAL by reaffirming its backing for Korean Air Chairman Cho Won-tae, bolstering the incumbent leadership's position in the escalating ownership battle, a Delta executive said Wednesday. "Delta is committed to the success of our leading trans-Pacific joint venture with Korean Air," Jeff Moomaw, Delta's vice president for Asia-Pacific, told The Korea Times in an interview. Cho is also chairman of Hanjin Group. "Delta owns 14.9 percent of Hanjin KAL equity. As a long-term shareholder, Delta is highly confident in Cho and the existing management team at Hanjin Group and at Korean Air." This strengthens Cho's position as Hoban Group seeks to expand its influence over the airline conglomerate. Hoban has so far expanded its stake in Hanjin KAL to 20.69 percent, rising to become the largest shareholder of the company. Cho and his related parties hold 20.58 percent. The official support from Delta carries considerable weight, as the construction group and its affiliates intensify speculation over a potential challenge

item.title: Lee calls for swift public housing supply to help stabilize market
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday called for the swift supply of public housing in a bid to stabilize the housing market. The president made the call during a meeting to promote public housing in Seoul's northwestern district of Eunpyeong, stressing the importance of speeding up housing supply and curbing real estate speculation. The remarks came as housing prices in Seoul remain prohibitively high following years of runaway price growth. The president said sluggish construction activity and a decline in construction permits between 2022 and 2025 led to a housing shortage, destabilizing the housing market. "It is important to expand housing supply and provide housing as quickly as possible," he stressed. To this end, the government plans to annually supply 240,000 public housing units through 2030, which he said would mark the highest level of home supplies on record. The president also stressed the importance of improving the quality of public housing, noting that it should serve as a stepping stone for people seeking to buy their own homes.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz bets on core models in EV strategy shift away from EQ lineup
item.description: Long associated with traditional luxury and prestige, Mercedes-Benz is reshaping its brand identity and electrification strategy to regain ground in Korea's fast-changing imported vehicle market, where technology and competitive pricing increasingly drive consumer choices. The German luxury automaker is moving away from its standalone EQ lineup toward electric versions of its established models, betting on familiar nameplates and next-generation technology to broaden its appeal without sacrificing its luxury heritage. Mercedes-Benz Korea begins customer deliveries of the all-new electric GLB on Wednesday, marking its third next-generation electric vehicle (EV) to debut in Korea this year, following the launch of the electric CLA and GLC in October. "Both of them are marking a very important chapter in our electrification journey here in Korea," Mercedes-Benz Korea CEO Shirin Emira said of the CLA and GLC during a test-drive event on the southern resort island of Jeju on Monday. Emira also described the launch of the electric GLB as "another vital milestone" in the brand's electrification

item.title: Samsung Display invests 210 mil. euros in ams OSRAM, becomes largest shareholder
item.description: Samsung Display, a Korean display maker, said Wednesday it has signed an agreement to become the largest shareholder in European chipmaker ams OSRAM. Under the agreement, Samsung Display will acquire 9.98 million newly issued shares of ams OSRAM at 21 euros ($23) apiece, for a total investment of 210 million euros. Upon completion of the deal, Samsung Display will hold a 9.1 percent stake in the company, making it the No. 1 shareholder. The investment will be accompanied by a strategic partnership between the two display makers to jointly develop and commercialize next-generation "ultra-small" microLED technology. "Ultra-small microLED is a next-generation inorganic self-emissive technology with the potential to overcome the limitations of existing technologies in areas such as brightness and lifetime," said Yi Chung, President and chief executive officer (CEO) of Samsung Display. Samsung Display said the partnership aims to secure core microLED component technologies, which are drawing attention as a next-generation display technology following organic light-emitting diode (OLED) displa

item.title: Colombia security forces storm site of supermarket hostage siege
item.description: CARTAGENA, Colombia — Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in the Caribbean city of Cartagena early Wednesday in a bid to end a day-long hostage siege, AFP reporters said. Several explosions were heard before security forces moved into the building, where about 20 people were believed to be held by armed men. Authorities said 10 of the roughly 30 hostages initially held had been released after hours of negotiations, including several elderly women. AFP reporters earlier saw a police helicopter hovering low over the building, before the assault began. President Abelardo de la Espriella traveled to Cartagena as the crisis unfolded and met security commanders at the scene. Authorities have said the siege began after an attempted armored vehicle robbery.

item.title: Dalsung County weaves 'The King's Warden' into tourism promotions
item.description: A promotional video produced by Dalsung County, Daegu won the grand prize in the historical and cultural category at the third Korea Local Government Promotional Awards. According to Dalsung County on Tuesday, the Korea Local Government Promotional Awards, hosted and organized by the Korea Media and Video Promotion Institute and sponsored by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, and the Korea Communications Commission, evaluates promotional videos produced by local governments nationwide. “The Man Who Lives at Yuksinsa” was created to promote Yuksinsa, one of Dalsung County's representative historical sites. The shrine houses the memorial tablets of the Six Martyred Ministers, who lost their lives while plotting to restore King Danjong to the throne during the reign of King Sejo of Joseon. The nearby Myogol Village is a clan village of the Suncheon Park family, descendants of Park Paeng-nyeon, one of the Six Martyred Ministers. item.title: Foreign ministry discusses support for Korean firms facing challenges in India
item.description: The foreign ministry said Wednesday it held a meeting with Korean companies operating in India to discuss their business activities and ways to address difficulties they face in the country. The meeting, chaired by Lee Min-kyung, director-general for Asian and Pacific affairs, brought together representatives from major companies, including Hyundai Motor, Samsung Electronics and POSCO, as well as experts on India, according to the ministry. Participants exchanged views on business conditions in India and raised difficulties and requests for government support. item.title: Alice Huang-linked firms listed $270 mil. in AI servers in China, records show
item.description: BEIJING — Companies linked to Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman whose affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang triggered his short-lived exit, raised financing against powerful computing equipment for major AI data centers in China, previously unreported records reviewed by Reuters show. The central-bank documents identify up to 764 AI servers and modules valued at $270 million, along with $31 million in equipment used to connect them into large computing networks. Much of the hardware was listed as located at a sprawling Shanghai data center originally developed under a partnership with Chinese technology giant Tencent. The records show businesses connected to Alice Huang's family and associates helped finance and equip China's AI industry, even as U.S. authorities investigated whether her Singapore-based company Megaspeed helped Chinese customers obtain restricted Nvidia technology. item.title: Unionized rail workers to launch work-to-rule campaign Thursday
item.description: Unionized workers of Korea Railroad (KORAIL) said Wednesday they will launch a work-to-rule action this week as planned, making disruptions to train services likely. The Korean Railway Workers' Union said the action will begin at 9 a.m. Thursday and last through Dec. 4, with rail workers strictly adhering to safety and other regulations, such as not driving trains faster to make up for lost time, refusing to work overtime and responding to passenger complaints in line with manuals. The union has demanded improvements to the employee promotion system, extra allowances and additional personnel, threatening to launch an indefinite general strike Dec. 10 if the needs are not addressed. It has said rail workers have operated train services on time through endless overtime and holiday work, as well as by working solo in dangerous environments, and that if working to rule leads to delays or suspensions, the effort will prove the lack of personnel. It has said rail workers have operated train services on time through endless overtime and holiday work, as well as by working solo in dangerous environments, and that if working to rule leads to delays or suspensions, the effort will prove the lack of personnel. item.title: [COVER STORY] Why spy agency chief nominee is under scrutiny
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung’s nomination of former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil as chief of the nation's top spy agency is drawing mixed reactions over whether she is fit for the position. Supporters say Kang is an apolitical pick with experience in leading a government organization and is suitable for a time of strained ties with Washington. Critics, however, cite her lack of intelligence experience and her alleged closeness to China. If confirmed by the National Assembly, Kang, 69, would lead the National Intelligence Service (NIS), an agency central to national security, at a time when Seoul’s ties with Washington are strained over several issues, including Coupang and intelligence sharing. The U.S. has been limiting intelligence sharing with Seoul, a move that is believed to stem from Washington’s suspicion that Unification Minister Chung Dong-young publicly disclosed intelligence on North Korea that Washington had shared with Seoul. item.title: KOSPI sinks 6% as chip outlook, US tariff concerns weigh
item.description: The benchmark KOSPI plunged more than 6 percent Wednesday, erasing the previous session’s rally sparked by the reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Shares of Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, which had surged on the news a day earlier, gave up all of their previous day’s gains, tumbling 9.87 percent and 11.05 percent, respectively. The sharp sell-off came as global investment banks cut their price targets for the country’s two semiconductor heavyweights, adding to concerns over the longer-term earnings outlook for companies that together account for nearly half of the index’s market capitalization. KOSPI opened at 4,809, down 3.94 percent from the previous close, according to the Korea Exchange. A sell-sidecar was triggered at 9:08 a.m., shortly after the market opened, temporarily suspending program sell orders for five minutes amid heightened volatility. This brought the number of sidecars activated on KOSPI this year to 62, more than double the 26 recorded during the global financial crisis in 2008. item.title: KEPCO offers up to $6,800 in fraud coverage after data breach
item.description: Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO), the state-run power utility, announced Wednesday a three-pronged customer protection package offering free identity theft prevention services and financial fraud insurance worth up to 10 million won ($6,800) to prevent further damage from a massive personal data breach disclosed last week. Under the measures, KEPCO is providing all notified victims with free one-year subscriptions to NICE Information Service's Jikimi Careship program. The service blocks unauthorized credit inquiries and identity verification attempts and provides compensation of up to 10 million won for financial losses caused by identity theft. Registration codes are being sent in phases via KakaoTalk, text messages and email on Wednesday and Thursday. Customers can redeem the vouchers through Dec. 31, 2027. The service automatically expires after one year, with no additional charges. KEPCO is also directing affected customers to AccountInfo, an integrated account management service operated by the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute, and Msafer, a free identit

item.title: Who is Kang Kum-sil?
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung's pick for spy agency chief, former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil, is drawing attention as she is returning to the main venue of politics after a decade out of the political spotlight. If the National Assembly confirms her for the post, Kang would become the first woman to lead the National Intelligence Service since the agency's predecessor was founded in 1961. Kang, 69, became the first justice minister under President Roh Moo-hyun in 2003. At 46, she was the youngest person and the first woman to hold the post. She remained the only woman to serve as justice minister until Choo Mi-ae, now governor of Gyeonggi Province, was appointed in 2020. Born on Jeju Island in 1957, Kang attended Kyunggi Girls’ High School and studied law at Seoul National University, long seen as the classic path into Korea's legal elite. She passed the bar exam in 1981 and served as a judge from 1983 to 1995. She was one of the judiciary’s leading progressive judges, co-founding the Uri Law Research Society in 1988 and helping lead major court reforms in 1993. After leaving the bench

item.title: 'Hanwha Group's spirit of challenge, Ourhome's expertise to fuel K-food growth'
item.description: Hanwha Group Chairman Kim Seung-youn has called for combining the group’s spirit of challenge with Ourhome’s food expertise during his first visit to the company’s research center since it became a Hanwha affiliate last year. “Let’s bring together Hanwha’s spirit of challenge and Ourhome’s strengths to create a bright future for K-food,” Kim wrote in the center’s guestbook during his visit Wednesday. Kim toured laboratories for food safety, flavors, home meal replacements and ice cream, reviewing product development and quality-control processes. item.title: AI could shorten CSAT's lifespan: Seoul education chief
item.description: Will artificial intelligence (AI) help hasten the end of Korea’s college entrance exam, with its heavy reliance on multiple-choice questions? Seoul education superintendent Jung Geun-sik sees that possibility, but teachers experimenting with the technology offer a more cautious picture of what it takes to change how students are taught and tested. Speaking at Tuesday’s forum on the future of assessment, Jung recalled his earlier proposal to abolish the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) by 2040. Recent AI developments and high-profile cheating incidents, he said, had led him to question whether the CSAT could even last that long. “At this pace, I wonder whether the CSAT will be viable next year or the year after. I had proposed abolishing it in 14 or 15 years, but the incidents surrounding this year’s exam have left me feeling that its lifespan may be much shorter,” he said. item.title: Finda to launch 'AI native' bank in Chuncheon
item.description: Fintech company Finda has chosen Chuncheon, Gangwon Province, as the base for its planned artificial intelligence (AI)-driven banking business, as it seeks to transform the operations of a savings bank it acquired earlier this year. Finda said Wednesday that it will relocate Daewon Savings Bank's headquarters from Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province, to Chuncheon following a shareholder meeting next month, when the lender will officially be renamed Finda Savings Bank. Finda completed the acquisition of Daewon Savings Bank in October, becoming the first Korean fintech company to acquire a savings bank. The move comes as the fintech firm seeks to integrate AI into the bank's core operations, including customer services, loan assessments and credit management. The company plans to launch a new service early next year, with AI agents handling routine tasks while employees focus on decision-making and oversight. Finda, a loan comparison platform, said the technology would help the lender assess borrowers' repayment capacity and creditworthiness, while allowing it to develop more digital-focus

item.title: Korea's crypto exchanges face ownership shake-up under new Digital Asset Basic Act
item.description: Korea's biggest cryptocurrency exchanges face a potential ownership shake-up as regulators move to cap major shareholders' stakes at 20 percent, or up to 34 percent with regulatory approval, industry officials said Wednesday. The limits were among the draft provisions of the Digital Asset Basic Act unveiled Tuesday by the Financial Services Commission (FSC). The proposal seeks to ensure that crypto exchanges serve the public interest, bringing them in line with capital market standards. Even shareholders cleared to own as much as 34 percent would face restrictions on voting rights above the 20 percent threshold. Most Korean crypto exchanges would fail to meet the proposed ownership requirements and would have three to six years to comply once the legislation is enacted. The proposal comes as Dunamu, the operator of Upbit, pursues a merger with Naver Financial through a comprehensive share swap. Dunamu Chairman Song Chi-hyung is currently the exchange's largest shareholder, with a 25.51 percent stake. Under the deal, which is subject to review by the Fair Trade Commission, Naver Financial

item.title: AMCHAM, AI policy chief discuss ways to deepen US-Korea cooperation
item.description: The American Chamber of Commerce in Korea (AMCHAM) held a roundtable with a senior presidential adviser on artificial intelligence (AI) Wednesday to discuss ways to strengthen U.S.-Korea cooperation in AI and advance Korea's ambition to become one of the world's top three AI powers. Ha Jung-woo, vice chair of the Presidential Council on National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, met with AMCHAM Chairman James Kim and representatives of member companies at the chamber's office in Seoul. Ha outlined the government's national AI strategy and key policy priorities, while participants discussed ways to strengthen the country's AI ecosystem through expanded infrastructure, including data centers, and advances in semiconductors, AI models and software. The discussions also focused on the role of global technology companies and public-private partnerships in enhancing Korea's AI competitiveness and accelerating AI transformation across manufacturing and other key industries. Participants explored opportunities to leverage the complementary strengths of Korea and the United States in AI technolog

item.title: First lady Kim watches performance by orchestra of visually impaired musicians
item.description: First lady Kim Hea Kyung on Wednesday attended a concert by an orchestra composed of visually impaired musicians, along with this year's college entrance exam takers. The concert, held in Incheon, west of Seoul, featured the Hyegwang Blind Orchestra, a group of around 50 visually impaired musicians, and was intended to encourage high school seniors who took the grueling college entrance exam earlier this month. The first lady attended the concert at the invitation of a student from Hyegwang School, an educational institution for visually impaired students in Incheon, whom she met last month at an event marking the 100th anniversary of the Korean braille system. Kim praised the orchestra's "enthusiasm and efforts" in creating harmony, while commending the high school seniors in attendance and expressing her hope that they would go on to make their mark in the wider world.

item.title: N. Korea closes Swiss office in Pyongyang over sanctions on children's camp
item.description: North Korea on Wednesday shut down Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang, calling on its head to leave "within 48 hours" over the European nation's sanctions on a children's camp in North Korea. The move came a day after Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of the North's leader Kim Jong-un, threatened to shut down the Swiss diplomatic office, which opened in October, over its sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp, which is accused of involvement in the forced deportation of Ukrainian children. Pak Hyon-su, director general of the North's foreign ministry in charge of the European department, summoned Astier Sylvain, head of the Swiss diplomatic office, and handed him a memorandum of North Korea's foreign ministry urging the closure of the office, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). North Korea's foreign ministry "declared head of the Swiss Diplomatic Office in the DPRK persona non grata and urged him to leave the country within 48 hours," the report read, using the acronym of North Korea's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. item.title: Korean firms eye foreign government, UN contracts at record procurement event
item.description: Korean small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are pitching their products to overseas buyers in one-on-one meetings in Seoul as they seek contracts with foreign governments, U.N. agencies and other public institutions, the Public Procurement Service (PPS) said Wednesday. The agency opened its largest-ever export matchmaking event, the Global Public Procurement Marketplace (GPPM), at Grand Walkerhill Seoul on Wednesday. Now in its 11th edition, the event runs through Thursday and brings together a record 378 Korean companies, up about 16 percent from last year, and 95 overseas buyers. The PPS is co-hosting the event with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and KEPCO Plant Service & Engineering. This year, the agency is helping exporters diversify their markets by pursuing contracts with international organizations. item.title: Top court to deliver ruling on ex-first lady's bribery case next week
item.description: The Supreme Court will deliver its verdict on former first lady Kim Keon Hee's bribery case next week, legal sources said Wednesday. The top court scheduled her sentencing for next Thursday after Kim and a special counsel team both appealed an appellate ruling that sentenced her to a five-year prison term on bribery-related charges, according to the sources. Special counsel Min Joong-ki's team earlier indicted Kim, the wife of former President Yoon Suk Yeol, on charges of receiving expensive gifts from multiple people in return for job appointments and business favors. The alleged gifts include jewelry worth over 100 million won ($74,400) from a construction company chairman in exchange for a government job for his son-in-law in 2022. A district court sentenced Kim to seven years in prison in June after finding her guilty on all counts but the appellate court reduced her sentence in September, acquitting her of some of the charges. It will mark the top court's latest sentencing for Kim after it finalized a four-year prison term for her in a separate case on corruption charges, including i

item.title: Popular military comedy 'New Recruit' to hit big screen with horror twist
item.description: Popular military comedy series "New Recruit" is heading to the big screen as a horror comedy featuring its original cast alongside K-pop girl group TWICE member Jeongyeon, who makes her acting debut. "While the TV series focused on sitcom-style humor centered on barracks life, I felt it was important to give audiences a clear reason to come to theaters for the movie," Min Jin-ki, director of the movie “New Recruit: Haunted Military Hospital” said during a press conference at a theater in Seoul. "To appeal even to viewers who have not served in the military, I focused on the keyword of military ghost stories." "I thought a horror comedy works best in a dark theater with surround sound, where both the scares and the laughs are doubled," he added. "Approaching a story set in a military hospital felt like something truly worth making into a film." item.title: Industry minister hints at exit strategy for fuel price cap
item.description: Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said Wednesday the government was considering a gradual exit from its fuel price cap introduced in response to the Middle East conflict, amid concerns over market distortions and the difficulties of compensating refiners for their losses. "When conditions allow, we intend to return gradually to normal pricing, potentially taking into account the differences between fuel products," Kim said at a press briefing Wednesday. However, he stressed that the government had yet to decide on any specific measures, adding that the price cap will remain in place for the time being as the situation in the Middle East continues to unfold. "We are not planning to take any immediate action. I was simply saying that this could be one of the options available as part of an eventual exit strategy," he replied when asked whether gasoline prices would be normalized first. Unlike gasoline, which is used primarily for passenger vehicles, diesel is used mainly in freight trucks and delivery vehicles. "When conditions allow, we intend to return gradually to normal pricing, potentially taking into account the differences between fuel products," Kim said at a press briefing Wednesday. However, he stressed that the government had yet to decide on any specific measures, adding that the price cap will remain in place for the time being as the situation in the Middle East continues to unfold. "We are not planning to take any immediate action. I was simply saying that this could be one of the options available as part of an eventual exit strategy," he replied when asked whether gasoline prices would be normalized first. item.title: Prosecutors seek to question Korean ambassador to China over alleged slush fund
item.description: Prosecutors investigating allegations that the family of the late former President Roh Tae-woo concealed a slush fund have asked his son, Ro Jae-hun, currently serving as the country's ambassador to China, to appear for questioning as a suspect, prosecution officials said Wednesday. The Seoul Central District Prosecutors Office recently issued a summons for Ro over alleged violations of the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment, among other charges, the officials said. Prosecutors are reportedly coordinating with Ro to schedule his questioning for around the end of this month. The prosecution suspects that part of a slush fund allegedly held by the late president's family was funneled into the East Asia Cultural Foundation and the Roh Tae-woo Center, both chaired by Ro. Roh, who served as president from 1988-93, died in 2021. The alleged existence of the slush fund came to light during the divorce proceedings between Roh's daughter, Roh Soh-yeong, and SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won. item.title: Prosecutors seek lengthy prison sentences for pastor, grandmother in fatal abuse of boy
item.description: Prosecutors on Wednesday sought a 25-year prison sentence for a church pastor on charges of fatally abusing an 11-year-old boy suffering from an intellectual disability. The boy died in August after he was strapped with metal chains to a bed at a church in Cheonan, about 80 kilometers south of Seoul, for 38 hours, during which he showed symptoms of high fever and exhaustion, according to the prosecution. At a trial at the Cheonan branch of the Daejeon District Court, prosecutors also sought a 20-year prison sentence for the child's grandmother for allegedly taking part in the crime, 12 years for the pastor's adopted son, and suspended prison terms of six months to a year for the pastor's younger sister and a church member. "The defendants abused an intellectually disabled child merely 11 years of age over a long period of time," a prosecutor said. "Though the boy showed symptoms of loss of consciousness and high fever, they did not take appropriate steps and caused his death, making the crime cruel and serious." item.title: Google, KBO team up to improve search experience for baseball fans
item.description: Google LLC said Wednesday it is teaming up with the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) to make the experience of searching for information online better for baseball fans in Korea as the country gears up for the regular season next year. Under the agreement, Google's search engine and artificial intelligence (AI) model Gemini will be introduced through the KBO's social media platforms, such as its official YouTube channel and Instagram, as well as live broadcasts of official matches. Google, on the other hand, will help fans search for information related to their favorite teams, such as information on athletes and past game results, integrating its technologies, the U.S. tech giant said. The two sides also plan to pursue various collaborations throughout the baseball season next year while planning to continue their partnership to provide colorful fan experiences based on the AI technology from Google, the U.S. tech giant added. item.title: Korean apparel makers bet on Central America as US tariff shifts squeeze margins: KIS report
item.description: Korean clothing contractors that make apparel for Walmart, Gap and Target are expanding production closer to the United States and building regional yarn and fabric operations as U.S. tariffs erode the cost advantage of their Southeast Asian plants. Korea Investors Service (KIS), a Moody's affiliate, said in a Nov. 24 report that heavy reliance on American buyers has turned U.S. trade policy into a major risk, along with rising wages, currency fluctuations and weak pricing power. While Southeast Asia remains central to their manufacturing footprints, companies are adjusting supply chains to protect duty free access and shorten delivery times. Hansae generated 94.9 percent of its 2025 revenue in the U.S., while Youngone and TP each derived about 60 percent of sales there, KIS said. Because those brands can spread orders across many suppliers, contract manufacturers struggle to pass along higher costs when trade rules or input prices change. Since April 2025, the U.S. tariff framework facing apparel suppliers has shifted repeatedly between country-specific levies, temporary global duties

item.title: Seoul public weddings surge 7.5-fold as couples seek distinctive venues
item.description: Seoul’s public wedding program has grown more than sevenfold over three years as couples increasingly choose parks, traditional Korean houses and cultural venues for personalized ceremonies that avoid the steep costs of conventional wedding halls. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that 563 weddings had been held or scheduled through its More Beautiful Weddings program as of the end of October, up from 75 in 2023, when the initiative began. Demand is continuing to rise, with 661 weddings already booked for 2027 as of October, surpassing this year's total. Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon met with three couples who had held weddings through the program and one couple planning to marry next April during a meeting Wednesday afternoon at Munhak House Seoul in Jung District. The gathering was intended to hear firsthand accounts of the wedding planning process and collect suggestions for improving the program. item.title: The cast and creators of 'SpongeBob SquarePants' look back on 27 years under the sea
item.description: LOS ANGELES — More than 27 years after “SpongeBob SquarePants” began airing on Nickelodeon, fans are still soaking up the enthusiastic sea sponge and his eccentric underwater neighbors. Even the actors, writers and artists who have worked to keep the animated series fresh without losing what made audiences fall in love with it in the first place can't explain why it has lasted so long. “It’s beyond luck. It’s not luck. It’s something crazier that we can’t really put our fingers on,” said Mr. Lawrence, who voices main antagonist Plankton and has written for the series since its earliest days. “I think most of the time I just always pinch myself and just go, I can’t believe not only that we’re working now, but that we hit on something that people are connecting with.” “SpongeBob SquarePants,” which has a new holiday special coming out Friday, remains the No. 1 animated show on linear television in the United States, according to the latest Nielsen animation report. item.title: Lee vows legal revision to punish domestic violence, even without victim's request
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung said Wednesday that his government will seek to revise the law to enable punishment for perpetrators of domestic violence even when their victims fail or refuse to file a complaint against them. The president made the remarks in a post on his X account to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, adding that it was the state's duty to create a society where women can live without fear. In Korea, perpetrators of domestic violence can avoid punishment if victims express a wish not to have them punished. However, the law has come under criticism over concerns that perpetrators may pressure victims into withholding consent to punishment, and that the lack of punishment could lead to more serious violence in the future. Citing a recent series of crimes involving domestic violence, stalking and dating abuse, Lee said the government had failed to "safeguard precious lives despite warning signs and calls for help." item.title: FM Cho calls on new KOICA chief to continue pursuing strategic development aid
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun on Wednesday called on the new head of the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) to pursue strategic, demand-driven grant aid programs. Cho made the remarks during a ceremony to present an appointment letter to Oh Hyun-joo, who was appointed as KOICA president last week, according to the ministry. The strategic approach aims to align the country's grant aid with its foreign policy priorities and partner countries' development needs while improving coordination among government agencies to enhance the effectiveness of aid programs. Congratulating Oh on her appointment, Cho expressed hope that KOICA would strengthen its role as a key partner of the ministry in coordinating Korea's grant aid programs and continue pursuing strategic official development assistance (ODA). Cho also called on the agency to develop "substantive, field-oriented projects that reflect the needs of recipient countries." item.title: Gov't reviewing various technologies to prevent AI-assisted cheating: minister
item.description: The government is reviewing various technologies to prevent cheating using artificial intelligence (AI) and other high-tech means, the science minister said Wednesday. Measures under consideration include communication and radio wave detection, watermark insertion on exam papers and behavior recognition using closed-circuit TVs (CCTVs), Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said during an event in Seoul. The ministry is also conducting a technical review on whether it could utilize jamming technology, or deliberate blocking of wireless signals used in special situations such as presidential security, but at a lower output, the minister added. On Seoul's partnership with global big tech firms regarding follow-up investigations of suspected cases of AI-aided cheating, Bae said the government is in the process of discussing the matter with such companies, whom he said "shared the same concern," on the AI-assisted cheating issue. item.title: Korea's 1st Embraer C-390 transport aircraft lands at Seoul Air Base
item.description: The Korean Air Force’s first Embraer C-390 Millennium military transport aircraft landed Monday at Seoul Air Base in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, after a delivery flight that included stops in India and the Philippines. Built by Brazilian aerospace company Embraer, the C-390 is Korea’s first military transport aircraft powered by turbofan engines. It will supplement the Air Force’s existing fleet of turboprop transports. The Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) selected the C-390 in December 2023 under a program to acquire three large transport aircraft. A defense acquisition official said the program has a total budget of 883 billion won ($657.4 million), with the acquisition contract valued at 710 billion won. The aircraft arrived on the same day that DAPA and Brazil’s defense ministry held their first joint defense industry committee meeting in Brazil. DAPA said in a press release Tuesday that the two countries signed a letter of intent to expand defense industry cooperation. item.title: S-Oil completes $6.9 bil. Shaheen project, shifts growth engine toward petrochemicals
item.description: S-Oil has completed its 9.26 trillion won ($6.9 billion) Shaheen project, reshaping its business portfolio around a larger petrochemical operation, as the oil refiner looks to secure a new growth engine beyond the volatile refining cycle. The refiner celebrated Wednesday the completion of the project and its 50th anniversary. Key participants included senior government and business officials from Korea and Saudi Arabia, including Korea's Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan and Saudi Aramco President and CEO Amin H. Nasser. Aramco is the largest shareholder of S-Oil. The Shaheen project, located at S-Oil’s Onsan refinery in the southeastern city of Ulsan, is the largest petrochemical investment ever made in Korea. The project includes a thermal crude-to-chemicals facility that converts crude directly into petrochemical feedstock. The project will help S-Oil add about 3.2 million tons of annual petrochemical production capacity, more than doubling the share of petrochemicals in the firm’s overall production mix from 12 percent to 25 percent. S-Oil plans to complete commissioning this year

item.title: Kookmin University design students win multiple honors at Clio Sports Awards
item.description: Students from the Department of AI Design at Kookmin University’s College of Design have earned recognition at the Clio Sports Awards 2026, a leading international competition honoring creativity in sports advertising. “Unseen Marks,” an individual project by Moon Seung-chan, won two gold and two bronze awards, the university said. “Flip for Safety,” submitted by a team of three students — Moon, Seo Eun-sol and Park Si-yeon — was shortlisted in the student design category. item.title: Mom's Touch shifts focus to franchising in Japan
item.description: Mom's Touch is shifting its Japanese business from company-operated stores to franchise expansion, targeting 100 outlets by the end of 2027 after establishing a foothold in the competitive market. The Korean burger, chicken and pizza chain began testing the market with a pop-up store in Shibuya in October 2023 before opening its first overseas company-operated outlet there in April 2024. Located at a site previously occupied by McDonald's Japan for 39 years, the store attracted 100,000 customers and generated 100 million yen ($627,100) in sales within its first 40 days. By its second anniversary, cumulative visitors had reached 1.44 million and sales totaled approximately 1.12 billion yen. Its average annual sales last year were 1.9 times those of a typical McDonald's outlet in Japan and 7.7 times those of a Mos Burger store, based on the companies' 2025 disclosures. Over the past two years, Mom's Touch has invested approximately 20 billion won ($14.5 million) in building its Japanese operations and developing a franchise model tailored to local demand. item.title: Seoul winter festival expands to Han River with 52 days of lights, markets and celebrations
item.description: Seoul will turn its winter nights into an expansive festival stretching from its historic downtown to the banks of the Han River, with 52 days of light displays, Christmas markets, performances and New Year's celebrations beginning Dec. 11. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that the 2026 Seoul Winter Festa will run through Jan. 31, 2027, across Gwanghwamun Square, Cheonggye Stream, Seoul Plaza, Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Bosingak Pavilion and Ttukseom Hangang Park. Last year's festival drew 10.98 million visitors, and organizers are expanding this year's program to include the riverfront while extending festivities through the end of January. Under the theme "Fantasia Seoul," the festival will bring together seven major events, including Seoul Light Gwanghwamun, Gwanghwamun Market, Seoul Lantern Festival, Seoul Plaza Ice Skating Rink, Seoul Light DDP, SeoulCon and the Bosingak New Year's Eve bell-ringing ceremony. item.title: SK Group chief's ex-wife opposes seeking court-recommended compromise for settlement: lawyer
item.description: Roh Soh-yeong, the former wife of SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, disapproves of his request to the Supreme Court to recommend a compromise for their property settlement case, her legal representative said Wednesday. Roh submitted a statement to the top court outlining her stance against Chey's request filed Monday, according to the representative. In his request, Chey voiced a willingness to pay the full 944 billion won ($700 million) in property settlement to Roh, as ordered by an appeals court, apparently stepping back from his appeal against the July ruling. "If Chey is sincere about an early resolution, he should immediately drop his appeal," Roh's representative said. A court recommendation of a compromise has the effect of a finalized ruling if the plaintiff and the defendant both do not raise objections within two weeks. Chey's representatives earlier said they were seeking a compromise recommendation for an "amicable and final end" to the legal dispute. item.title: Banks' household mortgage lending rates hit over 14-year high in Oct.
item.description: Banks' household mortgage loan rates rose for the sixth consecutive month to the highest point in 14 years and seven months in October on rising market interest, central bank data showed Wednesday. The average interest rate on new bank loans stood at 4.64 percent last month, up 0.07 percentage point from a month earlier, according to the data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The average rate on corporate loans increased 0.06 percentage point to 4.55 percent last month, and the rate on new household loans rose 0.06 percentage point to 5.02 percent, topping the 5 percent line for the first time since November 2023. The average rate on household mortgage loans increased 0.1 percentage point to 4.98 percent in October, extending its winning streak that started in May. It marked the highest level since March 2012, when the average household mortgage rate came to 5 percent. item.title: Hyundai Motor Group unveils unified EV charger ahead of 2027 global rollout
item.description: Hyundai Motor Group is preparing to bring a more consistent charging experience to electric vehicle (EV) owners worldwide, unveiling a new home charger designed to work across its Hyundai, Kia and Genesis brands ahead of an international rollout beginning in 2027. The HMG Global AC Charger consolidates designs and user experiences that previously varied by brand and market, the automaker said Wednesday. Hyundai Motor and Kia led product planning, technology development and design, while Hyundai Kefico participated in product development and will oversee mass production, drawing on its expertise in automotive electronics and EV charging systems. Designed primarily for home use, the charger will initially offer 7-kilowatt and 11-kilowatt output options in Korea and support the Type 1 (J1772) charging standard widely used in the domestic market. It will be available in both wall-mounted and freestanding configurations. item.title: Baemin delivery robots set to bring food orders to Seoul apartment doorsteps
item.description: Food deliveries in Seoul could soon reach apartment doorsteps without a human courier entering the building, as Baemin operator Woowa Brothers deploys autonomous delivery robots in residential complexes — including some of the capital’s wealthiest neighborhoods. Woowa Brothers said Wednesday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Tower PMC, a premium residential property management company, to expand its robot delivery service into apartment buildings, with a door-to-door launch targeted for next year. Under the agreement, the companies will introduce Baemin’s delivery robot, Dilly, to residential complexes managed by Tower PMC and develop infrastructure allowing robots to travel from restaurant entrances to individual apartment doors. The partners plan to select pilot sites in Seoul and install systems linking the robots to building entrances, elevators and designated waiting areas. item.title: Hanwha Aerospace wins export rights for KM3 amphibious bridging vehicle
item.description: Hanwha Aerospace secured the right to export the KM3, an amphibious bridging vehicle it builds under license for the Korean military, the company said Wednesday. The defense firm revised its manufacturing license agreement on Nov. 3 with Germany's General Dynamics European Land Systems-Bridge Systems, which developed the M3 system on which the KM3 is based. The revision allows Hanwha to sell the vehicle to some countries in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Nicknamed Suryong, the KM3 drives into rivers and either ferries equipment across or links up with other units to form a floating bridge, allowing tanks, self-propelled howitzers and armored vehicles to cross. Hanwha is the only M3 buyer that also manufactures the vehicle and the first to obtain export rights. The company has been delivering the KM3 to the Korean military since June 2024, and the vehicle recently completed field trials and deployment evaluations. item.title: Hyundai Glovis opens Incheon airport logistics center to expand air freight biz
item.description: Hyundai Glovis, the logistics arm of Hyundai Motor Group, has opened its own air logistics hub at Incheon International Airport as it seeks to grow its air freight business, the company said Wednesday. The company held an opening ceremony Tuesday for the Incheon Airport Logistics Center in the airport's second logistics complex. The five-story facility, with a total floor area of 44,420 square meters, broke ground in 2023 and went into full operation this year. It recently received customs approval to handle express import shipments, adding to its export cargo services. The center sits about 3 kilometers from the airport's cargo terminal. The center is equipped with automated systems designed for e-commerce shipments. Its first-floor express import clearance area can process more than 1 million parcels a month. Four high-speed X-ray machines can screen a combined 5,000 items per hour, with scan data sent to Incheon Airport customs in real time. item.title: Busan tourism portal lets travelers tweak itineraries via AI chat service
item.description: Travelers planning a trip to Busan can now ask an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to reshape their itinerary in plain language, such as requesting less walking on the first day, the city and the Busan Tourism Organization said Wednesday. The two upgraded the AI travel recommendation service on Visit Busan, the city's official tourism portal, on Monday. The service, first launched in September 2024, suggests customized courses based on trip length, travel companions and interests. The revamped version runs on generative AI built on a large language model, the type of technology behind chatbots such as ChatGPT. Users can keep chatting to shorten walking routes or add and remove stops without re-entering their trip details. A traveler who receives a two-day itinerary, for example, can type "Make me walk less on the first day" and then "Change lunch to a seafood restaurant," and the AI will apply the second request to the already adjusted schedule. Users can also add or drop places and change the order of visits directly on the itinerary. The schedule is displayed alongside a map showin

item.title: Tech-driven architect Carlo Ratti to direct 2027 Seoul Biennale
item.description: An architect known for exploring how digital technology, nature and human behavior can reshape cities will lead Seoul’s next international architecture biennale, bringing a distinctly technology-driven perspective to one of the capital’s major cultural events. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday it had appointed Italian architect and urban researcher Carlo Ratti as artistic director of the sixth Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism, scheduled for 2027. Ratti is a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Politecnico di Milano, where his work examines the relationship between architecture, urban planning, engineering and digital technology. He also directs MIT’s Senseable City Lab and co-founded CRA-Carlo Ratti Associati, an architecture and design practice established in 2002. His research uses urban data and sensor technologies to examine changes in transportation, the environment and public spaces, with the aim of understanding how cities can adapt to changing conditions. Recent projects include the Essential torch for the 2026 Milan-Cort

item.title: Korea takes regional tourism push to Shenzhen, turning APEC momentum into travel demand
item.description: From regional food specialties to beauty experiences and direct flights, Korea brought its local travel offerings to Shenzhen last week, seeking to turn growing interest in Korean culture into visits beyond Seoul. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Korea Tourism Organization held the 2026 Korea Festival in the Chinese city from Nov. 21–24, joining forces with the Korean Cultural Center in Hong Kong, the Korea Agro-Fisheries and Food Trade Corp. and the Korea Creative Content Agency. The event followed the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, using the gathering's momentum to promote regional destinations and encourage Chinese travelers to explore more of Korea. Shenzhen, home to about 18 million residents and technology companies including Tencent and Huawei, was selected as a target market for its young consumer base, whose average age is 33. Organizers designed the festival around Chinese consumers' growing interest in experiencing everyday Korean life, rather than simply visiting popular tourist attractions. item.title: Publishers pitch book rights to Italian buyers in online meetings
item.description: Korean publishers are pitching book rights to Italian and other European buyers through online meetings rather than traveling to Milan for a live showcase, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Wednesday. The ministry and the Publication Industry Promotion Agency of Korea are hosting the Visiting Korean Book Fair in Milano: Online Rights Meetings from Wednesday through Friday at a venue in Jung District, central Seoul. It is the first time the program, launched in 2015 to arrange one-on-one export talks between Korean and foreign publishers, has targeted Italy. The event was originally planned for Milan but moved online amid an unstable situation in Europe and concerns over rallies and a nationwide general strike in Italy. Seventeen Korean publishers, including Dasan Books, are taking part. Green Book Agency will represent 85 titles from publishers unable to attend. On the buying side are 47 Italian publishers and literary agencies plus five film and video producers and distributors. item.title: Seoul exhibition explores bold new possibilities for traditional hanok
item.description: Traditional Korean houses are being reimagined for modern urban life in a Seoul exhibition that brings together 12 award-winning architectural proposals and five completed projects, offering a glimpse of how an age-old building tradition could shape the city’s future. The Seoul Metropolitan Government will host the special exhibition, titled “Future of Seoul Hanok: From Imagination to Practice,” starting Thursday at Bukchon Cultural Center and Baeryeom House in Jongno District, the city government said Wednesday. The exhibition, running until Dec. 6, will showcase winning entries from the second Seoul Hanok Future Award design competition, alongside architectural projects exploring contemporary interpretations of "hanok," or traditional Korean architecture. A total of 70 teams entered this year’s competition, which focused on the Jeiggi-dong 988 area, where traditional markets and narrow hanok neighborhoods coexist. item.title: Yoon & Yang lawyer wins ALB Young Lawyer of the Year award for cross-border IP work
item.description: Kim Yoon-sun, a senior foreign attorney at Yoon & Yang, has been named Young Lawyer of the Year at the 2026 ALB Korea Law Awards for her work on high-profile intellectual property and cross-border cases, the law firm said Wednesday. The awards, organized annually by Asian Legal Business (ALB), a legal publication owned by Thomson Reuters, recognize the work of private practitioners, in-house counsel and law firms in the industry, with winners judged on the significance and complexity of the cases they handle. The Young Lawyer of the Year category honors a partner-level lawyer under 40 who has made a notable contribution to some of the year’s most significant deals or disputes. Kim was selected from a field of 11 finalists for her work on international disputes involving patents, trade secrets and the biohealth sector. She has helped develop legal strategies and coordinate proceedings across multiple jurisdictions in close collaboration with local counsel, contributing to the early resolution of a major U.S. patent litigation and favorable licensing agreements, according to Yoon & Yang

item.title: Global disaster misinfo fuels panic-buying at chain stores
item.description: Photos of bottled water, canned foods and spare batteries have flooded social media as consumers around the world stockpile emergency supplies in response to a wave of doomsday theories about an impending world war. To prepare for the intensifying strain of extreme weather and prolonged conflicts in Ukraine and Iran, countries such as the United Kingdom and Japan have recently advised households to check their cupboards to make sure they have at least three days' worth of essentials, from non-perishable foods to baby formula and first-aid kits. But the guidelines, which seek to prepare people for all kinds of hazards, have been embroiled in online rumour-mongering that has stoked public anxiety and panic-buying. Scores of social media users in the United States, Europe and Asia linked the updates to a spate of tech outages that disrupted flights and banking apps, speculating that another global conflict was just around the corner. item.title: Sejong University team assesses potential, limits of generative AI in crop breeding
item.description: A Sejong University research team has called for rigorous validation of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in crop breeding, saying evidence of their effectiveness in real-world applications remains limited despite growing expectations for AI-assisted agriculture. The team’s review, published online Nov. 4 in Molecular Plant, the world’s top-ranked plant science journal, examines the capabilities and limitations of generative AI and other AI-based breeding technologies. Led by Kim Kyung-do, a professor in the university’s Department of Integrative biological Sciences and Industry, the team conducted the study with researchers from the University of Georgia in the United States. The paper, titled “Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges,” was co-authored by Han Ji-heon, a Sejong doctoral student, who served as first author. Kim and University of Georgia professors Scott A. Jackson and Ethan Pickering were co-corresponding authors. “AI should serve as a tool to support breeders’ decision-making rather tha
