Their buttery scent will mingle with all the other aromas to form a dancing cartoon cloud of good smells, and everyone will marvel: You made bread from scratch!

item.title: POSCO International acquires US gas field for $550 mil.
item.description: POSCO International, the trading arm of POSCO Holdings, said Tuesday it has completed the acquisition of a U.S. shale gas field for $550 million as part of its growth strategy. The shale gas asset, owned by Chord Energy and located in Pennsylvania's Appalachian region, holds reserves equivalent to 1 million tons of liquefied natural gas (LNG), the company said in a press release. "This acquisition marks a significant milestone in the company's energy business in the United States, in line with POSCO Group's Triple Core growth strategy," POSCO Group Chairman Chang In-hwa said. "It will help enhance profitability by generating synergies with the group's LNG value chain, spanning production to sales." The company expects the shale gas asset to generate an average annual operating profit of 100 billion won ($74 million) through 2040 as it expands production. item.title: Korea's foreign ministry expresses regret to Russia over warplanes' KADIZ entry
item.description: The foreign ministry said Tuesday it has conveyed its regret to Russia over the entry of Russian military aircraft into the country's air defense zone and called for measures to prevent a recurrence. About five Russian military aircraft entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) over the East Sea earlier in the day and approached the edge of Korea's territorial airspace near Ulleung Island, according to the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS). "We conveyed our regret to Russia through diplomatic channels and called for measures to prevent a recurrence," the ministry said in a press release. The ministry sent the message to the Russian Embassy in Seoul but stopped short of summoning the Russian ambassador, diplomatic sources said. The defense ministry called in Nikolai Marchenko, a military attache from the Russian Embassy in Seoul, to lodge a formal complaint over the incident. The JCS issued an alert for residents of the eastern island as the aircraft appeared close to entering Korean airspace. The Air Force also scrambled fighter jets in response, though no violation of the count

item.title: Seoul Metro labor, management hold final talks ahead of planned strike
item.description: Labor and management at Seoul Metro, which operates subway Lines 1-8 and part of Line 9, began final negotiations Tuesday, a day before unionized workers threatened to launch a general strike. If the negotiations fail, the company's three labor unions plan to launch an indefinite general strike starting with the first trains Wednesday, potentially disrupting the morning commute. Seoul Metro's three labor unions are demanding a 3.5 percent wage increase, the scrapping of planned workforce reductions and additional hiring. Seoul Metro and Union 1 began their fourth round of collective bargaining and wage negotiations at 10 a.m., but the talks were quickly adjourned without an agreement. Union 1 is also demanding that the company scrap a plan to eliminate 2,212 jobs and hire an additional 1,313 on-site safety workers this year to address staffing shortages. Other demands include state funding for public services and a requirement that all field operations be carried out by two-person teams. Seoul Metro also held its separate negotiations with Union 3 and Union 2 at 11 a.m. and 1:30 p.m., res

item.description: POSCO International has completed its $550 million acquisition of a shale gas field in Pennsylvania, marking the company's entry into U.S. natural gas production and its first overseas energy asset acquisition since POSCO Group announced its Triple Core growth strategy in July. item.title: ASCC awards Fall 2026 In-House Scholarships
item.description:
By 
James Kneubuhl, ASCC Press Officer

Pago Pago, AMERICAN SAMOA — The American Samoa Community College (ASCC) makes available two “in house scholarships” open for application by all students at the College, one of which is also accessible to those who do not qualify for federal financial aid. The Division of Student Services, which administers the scholarships, has announced the recipients of the fall 2026 awards. 

The Presidential Merit Scholarship, for which US citizens and nationals may apply, has been awarded to Mr. Lama J. Petelo and Ms. Oloitefumalevaipaepae Wilson. The Saili le Atamai SGA Non-Pell Scholarship, for which students born outside the United States and its territories may apply, has been awarded to Ms. Ruiyi Shi and Ms. Kuinilena Lofipo. For both these scholarships, the award takes the form of a $500 credit towards the recipient's tuition and fees at ASCC.

Applicants for the Presidential Merit Scholarship must be full-time students in the previous and current semesters and have maintained a grade point average of 3.60 or better. They need to have completed 24 credits towards an Associate Degree at ASCC, as well as the classes English 150, English 151 and Math 90. Applicants must be U.S citizens or nationals.

Presidential Merit recipient Lama J. Petelo, age 19, graduated from Manu’a High School last year and now majors in Liberal Arts at ASCC Mr. Petelo, a member of the PTK honor society, has previously served as president of the College’s Nursing Club. In the words of Languages & Literature instructor Ms. Jayleen Chun, “Lama is a well-rounded individual who balances academic rigor with a respectful, kind nature. Deeply rooted in his Samoan values, he is always the first to assist his peers or support his instructors.”

Ms. Oloitefumalevaipaepae “Olo” N. Wilson, age 20 and also a Presidential Merit scholarship recipient, graduated from Tafuna High School in 2024 and is pursuing a major in Pre-Law. As of fall 2026, Ms. Wilson has the honor of currently serving as president of two of ASCC’s three honor societies, the longstanding Phi Theta Kappa chapter as well as the Sigma Kappa Delta chapter, which focuses on English studies. “Olo represents the ideals of scholarship, leadership, service, and fellowship,” said Mr. Kuki Tuiasosopo, lead faculty advisor of the PTK honor society. “She has demonstrated that academic excellence and community leadership can go hand in hand. Her willingness to take on responsibility and represent her peers reflects a level of maturity that is commendable for a college student.”

 The Saili le Atamai SGA Non-Pell Scholarship is sponsored by the ASCC Student Government Association and requires that applicants be full-time students in the previous and current semester with a grade point average of 3.0 or better, have completed 12 credits or more towards an Associate Degree or Certificate of Proficiency at ASCC, and have completed English 90 and Math 80. This scholarship is open for application by students who are born outside the United States and its territories who do not qualify for federal financial aid.  

Saili le Atamai Scholarship Recipient Ms. Ruiyi Shi, age 28, was born in China and graduated from Fujian Changle No.3 Middle School in 2016. Although she has only been in American Samoa since 2024, Ms. Shi majors in Liberal Arts at ASCC, is on-track to graduate this semester, and has been accepted to attend the University of Hawaii at Manoa in spring 2027. “Instead of seeing my international background as a weakness,” she reflected, “I have learned to see it as an advantage because I can understand problems from more than one point of view. I now want to continue my education at a four-year university and build a career where I can use both my Chinese background and the experience I gained in the Pacific.”

Also awarded the Saili le Atamai Scholarship this semester, Ms. Kuinilena Lofipo, age 19, was born in the Independent State of Samoa, graduated from Samoana High School last year, and is now majoring in Elementary Education at ASCC. “As a non-Pell Grant recipient who receives no financial aid, Kuini understands the necessity of working twice as hard to fund her education,” observed Ms. Aioise Talamoni of the ASCC Admissions Office, where Ms. Lofipo serves in a work-study position. She also drew commendation from Teacher Education instructor Falanika C. Timoteo, who said of Ms. Lofipo, “Her academic commitment, positive character, responsibility, and willingness to support others demonstrate that she will continue to grow as a student and as a future educator.”

ASCC Dean of Student Services Dr. Emilia Le'i expressed her pride in the accomplishments of this semester's four In-House Scholarship recipients. The Dean also encouraged any ASCC students who were not selected for the scholarships to continue applying. “In 2026 we’ve seen an increase in the number of applicants for the In-House Scholarships,” she commented. “We take into consideration the situation of each student, their record of academic achievement, and their demonstration of good citizenship through community involvement.” 

For more information on the ASCC In-House Scholarships, contact the Division of Student Services at 699-9155, ext. 0004.

item.title: Senator Muagututi'a, a dearly beloved father of the territory is mourned
item.description:
By 
Asi Andrew Fa'asau
andrew@samoanews.com

Pago Pago, AMERICAN SAMOA — American Samoa has lost one of its most outspoken, respected and loved leaders with the passing of Senator Muagututi'a Moevasa Tauoa, a veteran lawmaker whose wisdom, courage, and unwavering commitment to public service earned him the admiration of colleagues and constituents alike.

 Both the Senate president and Senate Pro Temp expressed their thoughts on the loss at the passing of the elder statesman.

SENATE PRESIDENT

Senate President Tuaolo Manaia Fruean, who was informed by family members of the senator's passing Tuesday afternoon in Honolulu, described the loss as a heartbreaking one for the Territory.

"The Territory has lost a man of great wisdom and foresight," Tuaolo told local media.

Those who served alongside Muagututi'a often spoke of his honesty and fearlessness. He was known for speaking his mind, whether addressing fellow lawmakers, cabinet officials, or leaders in government. He believed that public office carried a sacred responsibility and never hesitated to remind others of their duty to serve the people faithfully.

"When Muagututi'a spoke, we listened," Tuaolo recalled. "He never sugar-coated his words. He said what was on his heart and what he believed needed to be said. Some people did not always appreciate being scolded by him, but that was the old man speaking as a caring father who wanted the best for his people."

SENATE PRO TEMP

Senate Pro Temp Magalei Logovi’i Magalei expressed that the loss of Senator Muagututi’a has created a profound void, particularly in the chambers of governance, where his empty seat now stands as a somber reminder of his absence. 

Throughout his tenure, he was a source of wisdom and encouragement for those who served before the Senate, consistently emphasizing the importance of preserving and promoting our rich language, culture, and traditions. He championed the belief that these values should not only be remembered but also actively practiced and passed down to future generations. 

He said that Senator Muagututi’a was a passionate advocate for preserving and promoting Samoan culture and language throughout his political career. He firmly believed the essence of Samoan identity should be maintained and often discouraged directors and officials from using English when testifying at hearings, stressing the importance of communicating in their native tongue to preserve cultural integrity.

HIS LEGACY

Senators and regular viewers of Senate hearings streamed on social media will remember several occasions when Senator Muagututi'a Moevasa Tauoa spoke with the blunt honesty that became his trademark.

Whenever an issue touched on the dignity of the Fono or the proper conduct of public officials, he rarely held back, choosing instead to say exactly what was on his mind.

One such moment occurred in March during a joint session of the Fono.

At the time, Senate President Tuaolo Manaia Fruean informed lawmakers that Governor Pulaalii Nikolao Pula had requested a private meeting with him and House Speaker Savali Talavou Ale at Sadie's Restaurant. The Governor wanted to discuss the FY 2026 budget and the ongoing controversy surrounding funding for the salaries of unconfirmed cabinet directors.

Tuaolo told lawmakers he would only agree to the meeting if the Governor first removed his Chief of Staff, Leonard Seumanutafa. The demand followed a highly publicized confrontation inside the House of Representatives involving Seumanutafa and Vice Speaker Fetu Fetui Jr., an incident that had further strained relations between the Executive and Legislative branches.

While Speaker Savali initially expressed support for meeting with the Governor as requested, Senator Muagututi'a took a different view.

The veteran lawmaker agreed that discussions of such importance should not take place behind closed doors. In his opinion, any conversation involving the budget and other matters affecting the Territory should be conducted openly before the full Legislature, where all lawmakers could hear and participate.

He then turned his attention directly to the Speaker, delivering a rebuke that quickly became one of the most talked-about moments of that legislative session.

"Please, Speaker Savali, do not politicize this situation by meeting with the Governor privately," Muagututi'a said. "You have been doing that kind of thing ever since you entered the Fono many years ago, and you are still doing it. The Fono is the institution where matters affecting the wellbeing of the Territory are to be addressed. Stop it."

The chamber immediately erupted in laughter, easing some of the tension created by the senator's unusually direct remarks. Yet beneath the laughter was a serious message. Muagututi'a's comments reflected his longstanding belief that government business should be conducted openly and that the Legislature should never be sidelined when major decisions affecting the people of American Samoa were being discussed.

If there was one final moment that captured Senator Muagututi'a's uncompromising style, it came in September during a Senate session when he delivered what would become his last major public rebuke from the Senate floor.

The veteran senator launched into a fiery address in Samoan that evolved into an extraordinary condemnation of Governor Pulaali'i Nikolao Pula, culminating in a direct appeal to voters to remove the governor from office. For many longtime observers of the Fono, it was vintage Muagututi'a: blunt, fearless, and unapologetic.

His outburst was triggered by the governor's decision to dissolve the Board of Directors of the American Samoa Telecommunications Authority (ASTCA), a move that had already generated controversy and raised questions among lawmakers.

Addressing his fellow senators, Muagututi'a accused the governor of repeatedly disregarding the authority of the Legislature and acting beyond the limits of his office.

"I have monitored the Governor's actions from the beginning," Muagututi'a declared in a stern tone. "We should not be afraid to tell him that he has overstepped his authority because we put him where he is. How many times has he gone against the Fono's decisions? We should not be afraid of him."

In a dramatic moment, the senator turned toward the camera broadcasting the proceedings live to viewers on the Senate website and social media platforms and addressed the governor directly.

"Pula, if you are watching this broadcast, I'm telling you now that you are full of disrespect," he said. "I remind you that the government consists of three branches, the Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary. I am certain a significant amount of funds have been misused, and that is the reason he has dissolved the Board."

The speech then took an even more personal turn as Muagututi'a questioned the governor's conduct and leadership style, arguing that public office required humility, accountability, and respect for both the law and Samoan customs.

"Pula, you have been disrespectful and rude to the people of this Territory," the senator said. "This is what happens when someone who has been living off-island becomes a matai and is not fully versed in the responsibilities that come with that title, especially respect."

Muagututi'a also expressed disappointment over what he viewed as the governor's treatment of Lt. Governor Pulu Ae Ae Jr., questioning the dynamics within the administration and suggesting that elected leaders should place the interests of the people above personal or political considerations.

"Why did you select Pulu as your Lt. Governor and now you disrespect him?" he asked. "This is not your government that you can rule from wherever in the world you travel to. This is the government of Tutuila and Manu'a. We should elect a governor who truly cares for the people of American Samoa. Change the governor. Don't vote for Pula."

The remarks were broadcast live and quickly circulated across social media, generating strong reactions from supporters and critics alike. 

Some viewed the speech as an inappropriate personal attack, while others saw it as an example of Muagututi'a's willingness to say publicly what many were reluctant to express themselves. Samoa News understands many of his fellow senators also disapproved of his remarks, characterizing them as showboating by the Sua County senator. 

However, regardless of where people stood politically, few doubted the sincerity behind his words. 

Throughout his years of public service, Muagututi'a saw himself as a guardian of the Fono's constitutional role and an outspoken defender of government accountability. He believed senators had a duty to challenge authority when they believed the public interest was at stake, even if doing so invited criticism.

In many ways, the September speech embodied the qualities for which he will be remembered: a fierce independence, an unwavering confidence, a deep attachment to Samoan values, and a willingness to confront powerful figures head-on.

It serves as a final reminder of a senator who rarely measured his words and who, until the end, remained determined to speak his mind.

Within the Senate, Muagututi'a was regarded by many as one of the chamber's elder statesmen. His presence commanded respect, and younger lawmakers often looked to him for guidance. According to Tuaolo, his absence had already been deeply felt during recent Fono sessions while he was away receiving medical treatment.

A passionate defender of Samoan culture and language, Muagututi'a was a firm believer that the Samoan language should remain at the center of government proceedings. During committee hearings, he frequently encouraged government directors and officials to testify in Samoan, emphasizing the importance of preserving the language and ensuring that the work of government remained rooted in Samoan identity.

He was equally passionate about leadership and accountability. During confirmation hearings for cabinet nominees, Muagututi'a often reminded appointees that they were among the "birds of the flock" who had been sent away to gain education and experience and had now returned home to serve their people. His advice was straightforward and consistent: be honest, serve the public first, treat every employee fairly, and never show favoritism.

While his voice has now been silenced, the values he championed, respect for culture, honest leadership, accountability in government, and service to the people, will remain part of his enduring legacy.

A native of Faga'itua, Muagututi'a served the people of Sua County in the Senate for nearly a decade after first being elected in 2016 and subsequently re-elected to continue his service. He was serving in his third term when he passed.

The management and staff of Samoa News extend their deepest condolences to his family, the people of Sua County, and all those whose lives were touched by his leadership. May he rest in peace.

Local News
Tags: 
Senator Muagututi'a Moevasa Tauoa obituary

A passionate defender of Samoan culture and language, Muagututi'a was a firm believer that the Samoan language should remain at the center of government proceedings. During committee hearings, he frequently encouraged government directors and officials to testify in Samoan, emphasizing the importance of preserving the language and ensuring that the work of government remained rooted in Samoan identity.
He was equally passionate about leadership and accountability. During confirmation hearings for cabinet nominees, Muagututi'a often reminded appointees that they were among the "birds of the flock" who had been sent away to gain education and experience and had now returned home to serve their people. His advice was straightforward and consistent: be honest, serve the public first, treat every employee fairly, and never show favoritism.
While his voice has now been silenced, the values he championed, respect for culture, honest leadership, accountability in government, and service to the people, will remain part of his enduring legacy.
A native of Faga'itua, Muagututi'a served the people of Sua County in the Senate for nearly a decade after first being elected in 2016 and subsequently re-elected to continue his service. He was serving in his third term when he passed.
The management and staff of Samoa News extend their deepest condolences to his family, the people of Sua County, and all those whose lives were touched by his leadership. May he rest in peace.

item.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Nvidia on Monday said it is reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive, effective immediately. Nvidia shares surged on the news, jumping more than 25% in premarket trading. The company's move to bring Huang back marks a sharp reversal from its board's decision just days earlier to rule out his return. Huang built Nvidia from a video-game chip designer into the dominant supplier of AI processors, steering its chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties along the way. He resigned on November 12 after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman US authorities suspect of spying for China, an allegation Beijing denies. The board said it was satisfied with Huang’s candor and leadership ability and, after receiving input from senior U.S. government officials, saw no national security risk in his return.

Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow. item.title: Boy and elderly survivor pulled from rubble after Russian attack near Kyiv
item.description: Rescuers pulled a seven-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a residential building in the town of Dymer in Ukraine's Kyiv region as the death toll from Sunday's Russian attack reached 11, officials said on Monday. The survivors, who were trapped for 22 hours, were identified only as Davyd and Valentyna, emergency service spokeswoman Viktoriia Ruban said, without providing their full names. Doctors were treating the boy, who was rescued from the wreckage on Sunday, and his parents were with him, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday in a post on Telegram. He said four other injured people were also in hospital. Regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said earlier on Monday that rescuers had pulled another body from the rubble, raising the death toll to 11. The youngest of those killed was 11 years old, the Kyiv regional prosecutor's office said. Rescuers were combing the rubble of a residential building, after retrieving several bodies overnight. item.title: UK police evacuate 12,000 people from concert after 'unknown substance' release
item.description: LONDON — British police said they evacuated 12,000 people from a concert venue in Manchester after the release of an "unknown substance" required some in the crowd to be treated and one person to be taken to hospital. Police declared a major incident late on Sunday after staff at the Co-op Live arena alerted them at 10 p.m. (2200 GMT) that people in the crowd had fallen ill during a performance by U.S. rapper Don Toliver. The ambulance service for the North West England area said it assessed more than 50 people who reported "eye and respiratory symptoms," while attendees were quoted by the BBC as reporting a "horrible smell" and seeing people choking. Police said on Monday they had started an investigation to find out what the substance was and how the incident came about, after the ambulance service earlier reported the substance was believed to be tear gas. Tear gas is a chemical irritant that temporarily incapacitates people by burning their eyes, nose and throat. item.title: Iran says will use 'all available means' to counter US blockade
item.description: TEHRAN — Iran said Monday it would use all means at its disposal to counter a US naval blockade that was imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz. "We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter US aggression," said foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing. War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The conflict has since expanded after Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes across the region and with militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entering the fray. The Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies. In response, the US imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran. item.title: Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency during Nvidia boss affair: NYT
item.description: NEW YORK — Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China's top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant's former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. She was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence. Alice Huang, who is no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based tech group under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia chips, possibly in violation of US export controls. item.title: Ukrainian drones hit a Russian warship at a naval base in Libya, Zelenskyy says
item.description: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made sea drones in the operation, which struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship was one of Russia’s newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 invasion of its neighbor , the Ukrainian leader said in a post on X. Russian officials made no immediate comment. The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces. Ukraine has at times blindsided Russia during the war with ingenious attacks that embarrass Moscow, such as Operation Spiderweb in June last year, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked near air bases across Russia. item.title: Actor Ko Kyung-pyo appears for questioning over drunk driving, apologizes
item.description: Actor Ko Kyung-pyo presented himself for questioning Monday over allegations that he rammed into a cleaning truck while driving under the influence of alcohol, apologizing for what he described as an "irresponsible" attitude. The 36-year-old, best known for the hit series "Reply 1988," allegedly crashed into a cleaning vehicle in Seoul in the early hours of Nov. 14, while drunk driving. He has since issued a public apology and withdrawn from public appearances. item.title: 'Sumbakkokjil' producer serves Korean ghost lore to K-pop's global fandom
item.description: By pairing K-pop idols with Korean horror, "Sumbakkokjil" has grown from the first original program on Mnet Plus, CJ ENM's global K-pop platform, into its flagship, drawing fans around the world who tune in for their favorite acts and stay for the scares. "Sumbakkokjil" — the Korean name for the game of hide-and-seek — drops K-pop acts into abandoned buildings and other darkened sets. Group members must avoid being caught by an unidentified seeker for 4,444 seconds. In its first season, they hunted for keys before the chase began, while season two required them to collect "dead pieces" to escape. Rather than the typical showcase of singing and dancing, the show focuses on how idols react to the scares and how they look out for one another. Its second season, which wrapped Friday, made it the platform's first original to run for more than one season. The season and its related content was watched in 213 regions and drew more than 100 million cumulative views, and CJ ENM credits it with bringing in over 320,000 new sign-ups. item.title: SK chair offers to pay full $701 mil. to settle divorce dispute
item.description: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won on Monday asked the Supreme Court to propose a settlement in his divorce-related property dispute, offering to pay the full 944 billion won ($701 million) awarded by a lower court to his former wife, Art Center Nabi Director Roh Soh-yeong. Chey’s representatives said the offer was intended to bring the long-running dispute to an end, but it does not mean the case is over. If the Supreme Court proposes a settlement, either party may object within two weeks of receiving the decision. If neither party objects, the settlement carries the same legal force as a final judgment. The dispute began in 2017, when Chey filed for divorce from Roh, whom he married in 1988. The lower court treated Chey’s SK shares as his personal property and ordered him to pay Roh 66.5 billion won as her share of the couple’s assets. An appeals court in May 2024 ruled that Chey’s SK shares should be included in the division of marital assets and raised the amount he was ordered to pay Roh to 1.38 trillion won. The Supreme Court sent the case back to the appeals court for a retri

item.title: Korean, Mongolian FMs discuss cooperation on critical minerals, trade
item.description: The top diplomats of Korea and Mongolia discussed bilateral cooperation on critical minerals, trade, technology and other key issues during their talks in Seoul on Monday, the foreign ministry said. Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met with Mongolian Foreign Minister Batmunkh Battsetseg at his ministry as the two countries seek to expand cooperation following Korean President Lee Jae Myung's state visit to Ulaanbaatar in July. During the meeting, Cho called for accelerating joint efforts to sign a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA), noting that the agreement, if inked, would serve as an institutional foundation for expanding bilateral trade and investment, according to the ministry. Cho also noted the need for the two countries to leverage a rare metals cooperation center in the Mongolian capital for expanding cooperation across the entire critical minerals value chain. The center opened last December as part of Seoul's official development assistance project for the country. He also asked the Mongolian government to help ensure that Korean businesses can operate in the country

item.title: Nearly 3,000 people petition gov't to prevent cheating on college entrance exam
item.description: Nearly 3,000 people have signed a petition demanding the government take proper steps to prevent cheating on the national college entrance exam, a student-led advocacy group said Monday, amid controversy over artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating. The group, composed mainly of high school and college students, said it conducted two rounds of signature campaigns starting last Monday and a total of 2,964 people had joined the petition. Most of the signatories were students who had sat for the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on Thursday amid confusion over the government's announcement of haphazard measures to prevent AI-assisted cheating. The measures had been rolled out after the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam admitted to cheating using a miniature camera, a smartphone and generative AI. In the petition, the group said it demands the education ministry and relevant authorities clearly outline procedures for filing appeals and the criteria for invalidating scores in cases of cheating, among other measures.

item.title: 2-term lawmaker nominated to lead interior ministry
item.description: Rep. Han Jun-ho, tapped to lead the interior ministry, is a two-term lawmaker of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) who formerly worked as a news anchor. Born in 1974 in the southwestern city of Jeonju, Han graduated from Yonsei University with a degree in mathematics before joining local broadcaster MBC as a newscaster in 2003. He left MBC in 2018 and worked at the presidential office under then President Moon Jae-in as a communications official. Han was elected as a lawmaker for the DPK in the 2020 general elections before winning his second term in the 2024 elections. He currently serves as a ranking member of the parliamentary science, ICT, broadcasting and communications committee. "As a two-term lawmaker and a former journalist, (Han) racked up legislative experience in various sectors, such as land, transport and artificial intelligence (AI)," Lim Kwang-hyun, presidential chief of staff, said. "He is expected to robustly secure public safety and inject vitality into region-led growth."

item.title: Kim Myung-min returns as ruthless jungle boss in 'Tristes Tropiques'
item.description: For veteran actor Kim Myung-min, returning to the big screen after a seven-year absence did not feel like a long wait at all. "To be honest, I didn't realize it had been seven years until I saw it in news reports," Kim told The Korea Times at a cafe in Seoul, Monday. "Back when I was younger, even two or three years felt like forever. Now that I am in my 50s, time flies at the speed of light." Kim stars as Master in director Park Hoon-jung's upcoming action noir "Tristes Tropiques," whose French title translates to "sad tropics." The movie marks Kim's first movie appearance since 2019 and his first project since the 2024 ENA drama "Your Honor." It also reunites him with Park nine years after they worked together on the 2017 crime thriller "V.I.P." Set in a dense rainforest, the story follows a group of young assassins raised by Master, the supreme ruler of a killer organization specializing in jungle warfare. item.title: 3-term lawmaker with N. Korea expertise tapped as unification minister
item.description: Unification Minister nominee Hong Ihk-pyo is a three-term lawmaker and a close political ally of President Lee Jae Myung with North Korea expertise. Born in 1967, he studied political science at Hanyang University. Before entering politics, he worked as a researcher at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy and as a policy adviser to the Ministry of Unification. He also taught as a professor at the University of North Korean Studies. He won election to the National Assembly three times, serving from 2012 to 2024. Hong served as floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea from September 2023 to May 2024 when Lee was party chair. Earlier this year, Hong was appointed as senior presidential secretary for political affairs, handling coordination with the National Assembly and the political parties. At that time, the president described Hong as "reasonable and amicable," a lawmaker who "continuously practiced politics of tolerance and cooperation" in the belief that confrontation can be solved through "compromise and agreement." item.title: Critic-turned-presidential spokesperson nominated as culture minister
item.description: Kang Yu-jung, the senior presidential spokesperson nominated as culture minister Monday, is a cultural specialist who worked for nearly two decades as a film and literary critic and columnist. Kang, 51, first gained prominence in 2005 when she swept three prizes in that year's newspaper literary contests, winning in film criticism from the Dong-A Ilbo and in literary criticism from the Chosun Ilbo and the Kyunghyang Shinmun. As a critic and columnist, Kang regularly appeared on television programs about film and wrote for daily newspapers. She also published several books on cinema and taught at Korea University and Kangnam University. Her interest in the arts extended beyond criticism. Last year, she received a special award at the Korea Dance Awards in recognition of her support for dance and her contributions to developing and popularizing the art form. Kang entered politics in the 2024 general election, winning a proportional representation seat with the Democratic Alliance of Korea, a coalition party led by the Democratic Party of Korea. item.title: Ex-diplomat well versed in US, N. Korea tapped as foreign minister
item.description: Foreign Minister nominee Lim Woong-soon, currently a senior presidential security official, is a former veteran diplomat well versed in relations with the United States and diplomacy with North Korea. Since President Lee Jae Myung took office in June last year, Lim has served as the second deputy director of the National Security Office at Cheong Wa Dae, assisting the president in making key foreign policy and security decisions. His nomination came as South Korea's chief diplomat faces a host of foreign policy tasks, ranging from implementing security, trade and investment agreements with the U.S. to handling North Korea-related diplomacy and ensuring cooperation with China, Japan and other countries. Since entering foreign service in 1988, Lim has served in various posts at home and abroad, including as ambassador to Canada, deputy consul general in New York, minister for political affairs at the embassy in Washington, and other posts in Austria, Italy, France and Spain. item.title: Korea's exports forecast to exceed $1 tril. for 2nd straight year in 2027
item.description: Korea's exports are expected to exceed $1 trillion for the second consecutive year in 2027 on continued global demand for semiconductors, a state-run think tank said Monday. The Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade (KIET) forecast that Korea will post $1.32 trillion in exports in 2027, up 14.1 percent from this year's estimate of $1.16 trillion. The trade surplus is expected to rise to $455.9 billion next year from $377.8 billion this year. The KIET said exports are expected to expand 33.9 percent on-year in the first half of 2027, driven by increasing investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, while they are forecast to contract 0.7 percent in the second half due to a base effect and a correction in memory chip prices. As strong semiconductor exports are expected to boost domestic demand, the KIET projected Asia's fourth-largest economy will grow 3.5 percent next year. However, the KIET highlighted lingering uncertainties over U.S. trade policies, global AI investments and further developments in the war in the Middle East as possible downside risks. The KIET p

item.title: G-Dragon turns heads with long, flowing hair
item.description: BIGBANG's G-Dragon drew attention with a dramatic new hairstyle at the 2026 MAMA Awards, appearing onstage with long, silky, straight hair that seemed to get in his way as he delivered his acceptance speech. The K-pop star appeared alongside fellow BIGBANG members Taeyang and Daesung at Kyocera Dome Osaka in Japan on Saturday, where the group received the Music Visionary of the Year award. While the award marked a significant moment for the veteran K-pop group, G-Dragon's striking hairstyle became a highlight of the ceremony. Sporting long, flowing locks that framed his face and fell around his shoulders, the singer struggled to keep his hair out of the way while speaking. "My hair is giving me a hard time," G-Dragon said, drawing laughter from the audience. Seeing his bandmate's difficulty, Daesung playfully swept G-Dragon's hair to the side and said, "Go ahead." "We like to joke around a lot," G-Dragon said, adding to the lighthearted atmosphere. The playful exchange offered a memorable moment during an otherwise emotional acceptance speech as BIGBANG reflected on its nearly two decades i

item.title: Unification minister, Mongolian FM vow closer cooperation for peace on Korean Peninsula
item.description: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young on Monday asked Mongolia to support peace on the Korean Peninsula, citing its friendly ties with the two Koreas, during a meeting with Mongolian Foreign Minister Batmunkh Battsetseg, the ministry said. Chung noted Mongolia's efforts to promote regional peace and thanked Battsetseg for the warm welcome he received in June when he visited the country to attend the 11th Ulaanbaatar Dialogue on Northeast Asian Security. Describing bilateral relations as entering an "age of gold," he expressed hope that the two countries will keep deepening mutual ties. Battsetseg also vowed to continue close cooperation with Seoul in its push for peaceful coexistence on the peninsula, according to the ministry.

item.title: Seoul stocks lose 3.3% as AI rout tests gov't rescue plans
item.description: Korean stocks fell 3.31 percent Monday, as a sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI)-related shares deepened, though bargain hunting after steep losses and government preparations to activate a stock market stabilization fund helped limit the decline. The benchmark KOSPI closed at 4,708.54, down 3.31 percent, its lowest finish since Jan. 13. The index opened 2.77 percent lower and plunged as much as 5 percent intraday, briefly slipping to 4,586.8. A sell-side sidecar was triggered at 11:33 a.m. The index pared losses in afternoon trading to finish just above the 4,700 mark. Institutional and other corporate investors helped cushion the decline as foreign and retail investors continued to sell, according to analysts. The decline followed Friday's sharp sell-off on Wall Street, where Nvidia, Sandisk, Micron, AMD and Broadcom each tumbled more than 10 percent, sending the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 10.73 percent. The losses extended across Korea's AI supply chain. SK hynix fell 2.52 percent to close at 1,085,000 won ($807.05), while Samsung Electronics dropped 3.06 percent to 17

item.title: Intelligence rift with US could become security crisis if not resolved quickly, lawmaker warns
item.description: The ongoing restrictions on intelligence sharing between South Korea and the United States could spiral into a full-blown security crisis if not resolved quickly and Seoul must strengthen ties with Washington and Tokyo to counter the deepening North Korea-China-Russia axis, the chairman of the National Assembly’s Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee said. “Korea is currently experiencing dissonance with the U.S. in intelligence cooperation, which could escalate into a grave security crisis if not restored quickly,” Rep. Song Seog-jun of the main opposition People Power Party said during an interview with The Korea Times, Wednesday, noting that South Korea still relies heavily on military intelligence from both the U.S. and Japan. “We must solidify ties with our traditional allies so that South Korea can effectively leverage the mature and robust national strength it has built,” he said, adding that stronger alliances could compel North Korea, China and Russia to offer concessions. item.title: Former longtime SC Bank Korea chief tapped to head banking lobby
item.description: Park Jong-bok, former CEO of Standard Chartered (SC) Bank Korea, has been named the sole candidate to lead the Korea Federation of Banks, setting him up to become the next head of the banking lobby, the federation said Monday. The federation's chairman recommendation committee selected Park from its pool of candidates at its third meeting. It is scheduled to hold a general meeting Thursday to formally elect its next chairman. The committee said Park was well qualified to address the challenges facing the banking industry and help it navigate growing uncertainties, citing his broad understanding of the financial sector. Born in 1955 in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, Park graduated from Cheongju High School and Kyung Hee University's economics department. He began his banking career at Cheil Bank in 1979 and later served as executive vice president overseeing retail banking at SC Bank Korea. item.title: Stray Kids' Felix brings fresh energy to Korean hanbok
item.description: Felix of K-pop group Stray Kids is putting a modern face on traditional Korean clothing, called "hanbok," joining five local designers in a fashion campaign set to reach audiences in six major cities around the world. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Monday it had unveiled the 2026 Hanbok Wave campaign, featuring the internationally popular singer in a series of photographs showcasing contemporary interpretations of traditional Korean dress. The project, organized with the Korea Craft and Design Foundation, pairs promising domestic hanbok brands with prominent figures from Korean popular culture to reinterpret traditional clothing for modern audiences and promote it internationally. Their designs draw on traditional Korean aesthetics while introducing contemporary silhouettes, materials and decorative techniques. The collection includes layered garments inspired by traditional robes, coats featuring landscapes drawn from Korean ink paintings and designs incorporating mother-of-pearl patterns. item.title: S. Korea commemorates 16th anniv. of victory against N. Korea's 2010 shelling of border island
item.description: The Marine Corps on Monday held a ceremony to mark the 16th anniversary of South Korea's victory in an artillery attack in 2010 by North Korea on a border island that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The ceremony was held at Daejeon National Cemetery in Daejeon, some 140 kilometers south of Seoul, on the occasion of the 16th anniversary of the North's artillery attack on Yeonpyeong Island on Nov. 23, 2010. North Korea's shelling of the island marked its first attack on a civilian area in the South since the 1950-53 Korean War. During Monday's event, Vice Defense Minister Lee Doo-hee said the South Korean military will maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure its victory against any enemy threats. "Our military will immediately respond to any enemy threat or provocation and maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure absolute victory," Lee said in his commemorative address. "To achieve this, we will push to restructure the military system so that the Marine Corps will be enhanced to a quasi-fourth service," he added. item.title: Court holds arrest warrant hearings for 8 election officials
item.description: A court on Monday held arrest warrant hearings for eight National Election Commission (NEC) officials accused of manipulating voter turnout numbers or tampering with vote count records during the June 3 local elections. Three officials from the NEC headquarters appeared at the Seoul Central District Court in the morning, refusing to answer reporters' questions before entering the courtroom. Hearings for the remaining five officials from regional NEC offices were set to be held later in the afternoon. The court was expected to decide whether to issue the warrants later in the day at the earliest. Requests for the warrants were filed Wednesday by special counsel Lee Tae-han's team on suspicions that the election officials entered false voter turnout figures while voting was under way or forged vote count sheets during the race for the education superintendent of Gyeonggi Province, with some of them allegedly involved in multiple cases. item.title: Factional feud, impeachment fight test Kim Min-seok's DPK leadership at 100 days
item.description: Ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) Chairman Kim Min-seok heads into his 100th day in office on Tuesday, as party support slips amid a deepening factional feud, in stark contrast to the turnaround he promised. Kim pledged during his leadership campaign to raise the DPK’s support by at least 10 percentage points within three months. But a Gallup Korea poll released on Friday put the DPK’s support at 36 percent, down from 41 percent in a survey conducted from Aug. 11–13, just before Kim took office on Aug. 17. Under the circumstances, Kim’s leadership will face another test as he tries to reunite the DPK and win over centrist voters while the party’s hard-liners push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae — a move that could rally its base and alienate moderates. “It appears the voters still don’t feel they can count on the ruling party to settle problems under Kim’s leadership,” said Jung Jae-hwan, a political science professor at Inha University. “The move to impeach the chief justice will test whether Kim can keep the party focused on voters’ everyd

item.title: GS E&C joins hands with 3 firms to speed up data center construction
item.description: GS E&C has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with LS Electric, LG Uplus and Honeywell to shorten the time needed to bring data centers into service by coordinating engineering work from procurement through final testing. GS E&C announced Monday that the four companies had signed the MOU in Seoul. The construction company said rising demand for data centers amid the expansion of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry has made meeting customers' project schedules more important than ever. The partners will coordinate across four stages: procurement preparation, design, system installation and integrated commissioning. They will review power, design, construction, controls and operational requirements early in the process to avoid duplicated work and address operational needs before construction begins. The aim is to minimize potential delays during construction and commissioning so facilities can begin serving customers sooner. item.title: Lee Ha-nee met husband through unexpected matchmaker — actress Lee Hye-young
item.description: Singer and actress Lee Hye-young has revealed that she was the matchmaker behind actress Lee Ha-nee's marriage, surprising fellow celebrities with a previously little-known connection to the couple's love story. Lee shared the story during the Nov. 22 episode of SBS' reality show "My Little Old Boy," in which she joined entertainers Tak Jae-hoon and Kim Jong-min for a birthday celebration for actor Jung Joon-ho. Lee made a surprise appearance at the gathering, bringing Jung a painting she had created herself as a birthday gift. During the conversation, Lee, who hosts the dating reality show "Love After Divorce," said she had successfully introduced several couples. "I introduced Lee Ha-nee to her husband, and they ended up getting married," she said. "Her husband is a junior colleague of my husband." The revelation drew surprise from the other guests, shedding new light on how Lee Ha-nee, a former Miss Korea and prominent actress, met her businessman husband. item.description: The education ministry was set to file criminal complaints Monday against five people caught cheating with smart devices during last week's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), a senior ministry official said. The ministry previously announced that 111 suspected cases of cheating involving electronic devices were detected during the annual college entrance exam held Thursday amid growing public concerns over the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to cheat on national exams. item.title: Family of late LEET top scorer appears before police in cheating probe
item.description: A family member of the late top scorer of this year's law school entrance exam appeared before police Monday as investigators step up a probe into allegations that he cheated on the test. The late Lee Jin-woo, a 32-year-old dental student, was found dead Thursday after facing suspicions of cheating by using artificial intelligence (AI) to earn a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET). Despite his death, police have pressed ahead with the investigation on suspicion of fraud and other charges, after a group of lawyers earlier filed a police complaint. Earlier in the day, a family member of Lee appeared before the financial crime unit under the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. Police were expected to ask Lee's family member for cooperation in turning over evidence, such as his mobile phone. Lee's academic achievements came under widespread scrutiny following the recent admission by the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam that he had cheated with the help of AI. item.title: Hotel Shilla CEO Lee Boo-jin's son takes mother's surname after turning 19
item.description: The son of Hotel Shilla CEO Lee Boo-jin, a member of Samsung's founding family, has legally changed his surname to his mother's after reaching adulthood, following a court-approved application he filed himself. According to legal sources Monday, the Seoul Family Court approved a petition filed by Lee's son, Dong-hyun, to change his surname from Lim, his father's family name, to Lee. Presiding Judge Park Mi-hwa of the court's Family Division 21 granted the request last month. Dong-hyun reportedly filed the petition after becoming a legal adult in August. During its review, the court also sought the opinion of his father, Lim Woo-jae, a former adviser to Samsung Electro-Mechanics. Under Article 781, Paragraph 6 of Korea's Civil Act, a child's surname and ancestral family origin may be changed with court approval if deemed necessary for the child's welfare. Such requests can be filed by either parent or the child. Under Family Litigation Rules, courts may hear the opinions of the parents and children aged 13 or older when reviewing such petitions. item.title: 'Cats' unveils international cast for 8-city Korea tour
item.description: The international touring production of “Cats” will visit eight Korean cities beginning in December, bringing a 29-member cast whose performances combine singing with the demanding physical work of transforming into felines. The tour opens at Daegu’s Keimyung Art Center on Dec. 18 and continues through April 11, 2027, concluding at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts in Seoul, according to a press release announcing the cast and itinerary, Monday. The principal performers have traveled with the production since its South African opening in December 2025, followed by the musical’s Mumbai premiere and engagements in Hong Kong and Singapore. Cindy-Ann Abrahams will play Grizabella, the faded glamour cat. A semifinalist on “South Africa’s Got Talent” in 2013, Abrahams won a best actress honor at the Cape Town Theatre Awards for the role, according to the release. Dylan Janse van Rensburg will portray the rebellious Rum Tum Tugger. His previous musical theater credits include Joseph in “Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat” and Melchior in “Spring Awakening.

item.title: Korea's gender wage gap remains widest among OECD members
item.description: Korea continued to have the widest gender pay gap among OECD countries in 2025, with women's median earnings 27.8 percent lower than men's, data showed Monday. According to the latest OECD data, women's median earnings in Korea stood at 72.2 percent of men's last year. The gap was the largest among 13 OECD countries that have released figures for 2025, exceeding Japan's 20.1 percent and the United States' 17.9 percent. The figures for Korea cover full-time employees and compare median monthly earnings. They do not adjust for differences in occupations or job assignments. Korea has recorded the widest gender pay gap among OECD members every year since 2000, although the disparity has gradually narrowed. The gap fell from 37.2 percent in 2015 to 31.5 percent in 2020 and 29.3 percent in 2023. It narrowed further to 29 percent in 2024 and 27.8 percent last year. The wage disparity also varied significantly across income levels, with Korea recording one of the widest gaps among OECD countries at both ends of the wage distribution. item.title: Ex-Justice Minister Kang tapped as spy agency chief
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung nominated former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil to head the National Intelligence Service (NIS), Monday. Lee also tapped Lim Woong-soon, his second deputy national security adviser and a former ambassador to Canada, as foreign minister, and Hong Ihk-pyo, a former presidential secretary for political affairs and former floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), as unification minister. Presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun announced the Cabinet reshuffle largely focused on the security and diplomacy sectors during a briefing at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul. He said the changes would bring in new leadership to protect Korea’s interests as the international landscape shifts. “Kang is the most suitable person to reinforce democratic oversight of the NIS, based on her strong belief in the neutrality of powerful organizations. She is also expected to resolve new security threats, such as cyberattacks, through international cooperation,” the chief of staff said. item.title: Korea ready to deploy market stabilization fund if conditions warrant: finance minister
item.description: Korea will decide whether to deploy its stock market stabilization fund based on how market conditions evolve, Minister of Finance and Economy Lee Hyoung-il said Monday, a day after the government began preparations. Lee said the government would continue to monitor the market before deciding on the timing and size of any deployment. “We are reviewing the steps needed in case market conditions warrant activating the fund,” Lee said at a press conference. “We will decide on the details as we assess how the situation evolves.” Lee said the review was intended to ensure the fund could be deployed smoothly if needed, given how long it had been idle. Asked whether the government would expand the fund, he said authorities would assess market conditions at the time of any deployment before deciding on its size. His remarks came as growing doubts about the outlook for artificial intelligence (AI) and returns on AI investment dented investor confidence. item.title: NC raises 2026 sales forecast on Lineage Classic success
item.description: Korean game developer NC raised its sales forecast for this year to 2.8 trillion won ($2.09 billion) in a Nov. 11 regulatory filing after sales through September surpassed the lower end of its previous full-year guidance, as Lineage Classic and casual mobile games bolstered its results. Third-quarter sales rose 91 percent from a year earlier to 687 billion won, while the company returned to operating profitability, posting an operating profit of 120 billion won. Sales for the first nine months rose 83 percent to 2.01 trillion won, above the previous guidance floor of 2 trillion won. Lineage Classic generated 159 billion won in sales in the third quarter, bringing its cumulative sales to 428 billion won in about eight months after launch. NC said the number of paying players remained stable. Sales from casual mobile games rose from the previous quarter to 172 billion won, accounting for 25 percent of total sales. item.title: Daily share buyback limit to be lifted for 3 months amid market rout
item.description: The country's financial regulator said Monday it will lift the daily share buyback limit for listed firms for three months, as part of efforts to stem market volatility. According to the Financial Services Commission (FSC), the daily limit for the purchase of own shares by publicly traded companies will be fully lifted from Tuesday. On Sunday, the financial authorities announced a set of measures to limit market jitters caused by rising fears over artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments. They also said around 10 trillion won ($7.42 billion) worth of a stock stabilization fund is in store to be activated when necessary. If the market rout deepens, the fund will go into operation, marking the first time since 2008. Also, the authorities stressed that market monitoring will be enhanced and illegal short selling will be strictly banned. The country's benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index dipped as low as more than 5 percent, before recovering to some degree as AI optimism faded over valuations and rising debt.

item.title: Jongno District deploys AI crosswalks to give slower pedestrians more time
item.description: Jongno District in central Seoul is upgrading its intersections with artificial intelligence (AI), pavement-level LED lights and automated voice alerts to help pedestrians — especially children and older adults — cross streets more safely. The district office said it will begin operating pavement-mounted pedestrian signals and voice guidance devices at 123 locations from Dec. 1 with an AI-powered system that automatically extends crossing time. The pavement-level pedestrian signals illuminate the tactile pavers, a kind of ground surface indicator to assist disabled pedestrians, at crosswalks to help people detect when it is safe to cross. Voice guidance devices use infrared sensors to detect pedestrians and issue audible warnings when they attempt to cross against the signal, as well as announcing when the light turns green. The installations target roads with at least four lanes, prioritizing areas with heavy pedestrian traffic and a history of accidents. item.title: Trump hosts gala for meme coin investors as his token plunges to record lows
item.description: NEW YORK — US President Donald Trump has made hundreds of millions from his $TRUMP meme coin, but at a Sunday dinner for the token's biggest holders, he said his motive for supporting the cryptocurrency was to boost the economic competitiveness of the United States. “I’m doing it for the United States... If we don’t do it, China’s going to do it,” Trump told attendees at his golf club outside Washington. It was the third time Trump had held a gala for the top owners of his meme coin, which once soared as high as $75 but has fallen to a record low of under $1. The private dinner this year was more low-key than the initial event last year, attendees said, with a smaller crowd and far less money at stake this time. Attendees qualified for the dinner based on their time-weighted holdings of the $TRUMP coin from September 30 to November 16. Organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets met the criteria for Sunday's dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets when the contest concluded on November 16. item.title: US Forces Korea deploys Apache, Blackhawk helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan
item.description: The U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) recently deployed its helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan, the first time such assets have been sent outside the Korean Peninsula for exercises, the USFK said Monday. The 2nd Infantry Division's 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade deployed the AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, the UH-60 Black Hawk multirole utility helicopters and the CH-47 Chinook transport helicopters to the Combined Arms Training Center (CATC) at Camp Fuji, located in Shizuoka Prefecture, the USFK said in a social media post. It said the "historic first" deployment of the choppers was aimed at strengthening its readiness in the Indo-Pacific. The AH-64 Apache serves as a heavily armed attack helicopter designed to hunt and destroy enemy tanks and armored vehicles with missiles and rockets, while the UH-60 Black Hawk is a core asset primarily tasked with airlifting troops into combat zones, transporting supplies and evacuating wounded soldiers. The CH-47 Chinook is a heavy-lift transport helicopter used to move large numbers of troops, heavy artillery and bulk supplies across the battlefield.

item.title: PPP files petition with Constitutional Court over special counsel bill
item.description: Lawmakers of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) filed a petition with the Constitutional Court on Monday, arguing that their rights to vote on legislation were violated by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK)'s unilateral passage of a special counsel bill. The PPP's move came after the DPK-controlled National Assembly railroaded the bill earlier this month that mandates a special counsel investigation into suspicions that prosecutors under the previous administration had indicted President Lee Jae Myung and others on fabricated evidence. PPP lawmakers had boycotted the vote in protest. The PPP claimed that its lawmakers were not given sufficient time to review and deliberate on the details of the bill before its passage and said it filed a competence dispute against National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik and DPK Rep. item.title: New Incheon airport chief tasked with fast-tracking capacity expansion
item.description: Incheon International Airport Corp.'s (IIAC) new CEO Park Nam-chun faces the task of accelerating capacity expansion at the country’s main aviation hub, as passenger traffic is expected to outstrip existing infrastructure in the coming years. Park officially took office Monday as the airport operator’s 11th chief for a three-year term, with expanding airport facilities expected to be among his top priorities. The Incheon airport plans to add a third passenger terminal and a fifth runway to raise its annual passenger-handling capacity from 106 million to 131 million. Park’s key challenge will be to move the projects from planning to construction and operation as quickly as possible, with passenger demand nearing the airport’s existing capacity. The airport handled 74.07 million international and domestic passengers last year, the highest annual figure since its opening in 2001. item.title: KB Financial's new chairman sets sights on turning banking giant into global platform
item.description: Lee Jae-keun, the new chairman of KB Financial Group, set a goal Monday to turn Korea’s largest financial group from a “leading bank” into a “leading platform.” His plan calls for closer cooperation among the group’s 11 affiliates and greater use of data and artificial intelligence (AI), as KB seeks to move beyond its reliance on banking and compete with major platforms in global markets. At his inauguration ceremony at KB Kookmin Bank headquarters in Yeouido, Seoul, Lee said the advantages that once made KB a domestic market leader were no longer enough to ensure its future growth. “KB became the country’s leading bank through its sheer scale — its extensive branch network and large deposit and lending businesses,” he said. “But as AI and digital technology drive down the cost of reaching customers, the competitive edge built on scale alone is quickly disappearing.” KB Financial has delivered record earnings under outgoing Chairman Yang Jong-hee, reporting net profit of 5.79 trillion won ($4.3 billion) in the first nine months of this year, up 13.1 percent from a

item.title: Seoul launches green bio hub to connect startups with investors, global markets
item.description: Seoul is expanding its ambitions in biotechnology, transforming its food startup center into a platform designed to connect promising agricultural and food technology companies with major corporations, investors and global distribution networks. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday it had relaunched the Seoul Food Startup Center as the Seoul Green Bio Hub, broadening its focus from food manufacturing and distribution to technology-driven businesses built around agricultural and biological resources. Green biotechnology applies biological technologies to agricultural and other biological resources to create new products and commercial opportunities in sectors including food and agriculture. Of the 884 green bio companies registered nationwide with the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, 89 are based in Seoul, according to the city. item.title: Korea conducts evacuation drills in Latvia amid political uncertainty
item.description: Korea has conducted mock drills to practice evacuating and protecting its nationals in Latvia amid deepening political uncertainty in the Baltic country, Seoul's foreign ministry said Monday. The drills involving a rapid response team took place at the Korean Embassy in Riga on Friday, it said, as Latvia has experienced political uncertainty since its ruling coalition collapsed in May following a dispute over drone incursions, with the newly formed government holding a narrow parliamentary majority. Embassy staff, National Fire Agency officials and civilian experts participated in the drills, sharing information on the situation in Latvia and safety guidelines on how to respond to incidents and accidents, and checking communication lines. "The drills ... were very helpful in checking a coordination mechanism between the foreign ministry and the overseas diplomatic mission in case of a crisis, and strengthening the embassy's readiness posture for protecting citizens abroad," Korean Ambassador to Latvia Kim Jong-han said.

item.title: Industry minister urges petrochem sector to rev up restructuring
item.description: The industry minister said Monday the petrochemical sector should accelerate its restructuring efforts to enhance its competitiveness. In August last year, 16 petrochemicals companies drew up business reorganization plans. Two restructuring schemes were approved by the government earlier this year, but a business reorganization plan for the Ulsan industrial complex has not been finalized. In a meeting with heads of major petrochemicals companies, such as LG Chem Ltd. and GS-Caltex Corp., Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan urged petrochemicals companies to draw up their final restructuring plans. "All companies should share the responsibility for the future of the sector," Kim said, adding that all discussions should be done before the end of the year. Kim said all necessary measures will be provided to help the sector take a leap forward to remain competitive. The local petrochemical sector has been facing a prolonged oversupply leading to low prices, especially amid the economic slowdown. item.title: Japanese cultural envoy says people-to-people ties must go beyond gov't-level diplomacy
item.description: SUWON, Gyeonggi Province — Audiences gasped and applauded as Japanese magician Taiju Fujiyama pulled eggs out of an apparently empty pocket, performing Edo Tezuma, a traditional Japanese form of magic preserved for roughly 300 years. The performance was part of the 2026 Suwon Japan Week, organized by the Japanese Embassy in Korea to showcase traditional culture and arts. The event began on Friday and runs through Nov. 26 in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province, in line with the city’s 2026-2027 Visit Suwon Year. This year's program features a range of cultural activities, including traditional Japanese clothing experiences and traditional candy-making demonstrations. The Suwon Museum of Art is hosting an exhibition of ukiyo-e, a traditional Japanese woodblock print art form that emerged in the early 18th century, where visitors can view works by Katsushika Hokusai, one of the most celebrated ukiyo-e artists of the late Edo period. item.title: Seoul, Daesang turn tofu byproduct into healthier traditional snacks
item.description: Seoul is turning a byproduct of tofu production into a selling point for healthier snacks, teaming up with food company Daesang to launch two products that pair traditional flavors with waste-reducing food innovation. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday it introduced Seoul Yakgwa and Seoul GO Guma Bar, marking its first collaboration with a private company to incorporate upcycled food ingredients into products under its Seoul My Soul city brand. Food upcycling involves transforming ingredients and byproducts that might otherwise be discarded during food production into new food products, helping reduce waste and make better use of resources. Seoul Yakgwa reimagines "yakgwa," a traditional Korean honey pastry, using soybean pulp left over from tofu production, an ingredient rich in protein and dietary fiber. Rather than deep-frying the pastries, the product is oven-baked for a softer texture, while allulose is used to reduce sugar content. item.title: HD KSOE wins $228.6 mil. order for 2 LPG carriers
item.description: HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (KSOE) said Monday it has secured a 308.4 billion-won ($228.6 million) order for two liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carriers. HD KSOE, the shipbuilding subholding company of HD Hyundai, said its affiliate, HD Hyundai Samho, will build the vessels for an Asian client and deliver them by the first half of 2030. With the latest contract, HD KSOE has secured orders worth $22.1 billion for 201 vessels so far this year, achieving 94.9 percent of its annual order target.

item.title: Chinese man gets suspended sentence for stealing 100 BTS concert wristbands to resell
item.description: A Chinese man in his 40s has received a suspended prison sentence for stealing 100 admission wristbands at a BTS concert venue in Busan with the intention of reselling them at inflated prices. According to legal sources Sunday, the Busan District Court sentenced the man, identified only as A, to 18 months in prison, suspended for three years, on charges of aggravated theft. The man was charged with stealing 100 admission wristbands from an event booth set up at the Busan Asiad Auxiliary Stadium in Yeonje District, Busan, at around noon on June 12, along with two unidentified accomplices. According to the court ruling, A arrived at Incheon International Airport the day before the theft and met with two accomplices to plan the resale of BTS concert tickets at inflated prices. However, the concert organizer had introduced measures to prevent ticket scalping, requiring attendees to present identification matching their mobile tickets before receiving admission wristbands. item.title: 15 years, 164 awards: How Global Korea Award tracked changing Korea
item.description: In 2012, The Korea Times established the Korea Multicultural Youth Awards to encourage students from multicultural families who struggle with cultural differences and language barriers. Rebranded as the Global Korea Awards last year, the program marks its 15th anniversary this year. Over that span, it has recognized 152 students and individuals and 12 volunteer groups, teachers and institutions, distributing 164 awards in total. The Ministry of Gender Equality and Family has sponsored the program since its founding, and the grand prize winner receives the minister’s award. Among the honors is the Semoon Chang Award for students with outstanding foreign language skills, created in 2015 with column fees donated by Chang Se-moon, a former Korea Times columnist and retired economics professor at the University of South Alabama. Global Korea Award winners have played a key part in Korea’s multicultural youth community and continue to make their mark across a wide range of fields. item.title: Seven Luck casino operator GKL ranks No. 2 globally for ESG disclosure
item.description: Grand Korea Leisure (GKL), the state-run operator of Korea's foreigner-only Seven Luck casinos, won top honors for its 2025 sustainability report at an international communications competition, scoring 99 out of 100 to rank second worldwide. GKL said Monday that its report received the Platinum Award in the sustainability report category of the 2025/26 LACP Spotlight Awards, organized by the U.S.-based League of American Communications Professionals (LACP). The annual competition evaluates corporate annual reports and sustainability reports from around the world, attracting about 500 companies and organizations each year. This year's Korean participants included GKL, NongHyup, Hankook Tire, Dongkuk Steel, Binggrae, Lotte and SK Telecom, among more than 40 companies. item.title: Sungkyunkwan University team develops ultrasensitive vitamin C sensor using AI
item.description: A Sungkyunkwan University research team has developed an ultrasensitive sensor capable of detecting even trace amounts of vitamin C by using artificial intelligence (AI) to optimize sensor fabrication conditions. The team was led by Park Jin-sung, a professor in the Department of Bio-Mechatronics Engineering, according to the university. Other researchers included Park Daeil, Choi Do-eun, Jo Won-jun, Kim Chi-hyun and Park Joo-hyung. Rather than conducting numerous trial-and-error experiments, the team used AI to identify promising fabrication conditions based on a relatively small dataset and then verified the sensor's performance through actual experiments. The findings were published online on Nov. 9 in the Chemical Engineering Journal, under the title “Data-driven multi-parameter optimization of molecularly imprinted polymers for pico-level vitamin C detection.” “The most significant aspect of this study is that AI can help identify optimal sensor fabrication conditions without having to conduct a large number of experiments one by one,” professor Park said. “We hope to apply

item.title: CJ ONE offers foreign tourists free coupon package for Korea trips
item.description: Foreign tourists visiting Korea can now score discounts on everything from pastries and convenience-store snacks to beauty treatments and duty-free shopping through a free coupon package from CJ ONE, a major Korean retail and lifestyle rewards platform. item.title: Buick opens Electra E7 orders, targets Korea's premium SUV market
item.description: General Motors’ (GM) premium brand Buick said Monday it had opened preorders for the Electra E7, its first model in Korea, with prices starting at 43.6 million won ($32,500). The initial ordering period, which began on Monday, is reserved for customers who previously registered for advance reservations, while orders from the general public will open Wednesday. The Electra E7 is a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) combining a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated gasoline engine with an electric motor, delivering a maximum electric driving range of up to 126 kilometers and a total driving range exceeding 1,000 kilometers. Customers can choose between two lithium iron phosphate battery options, with capacities of 19.7 kilowatt-hours and 31.7 kilowatt-hours, offering certified electric-only ranges of 80 kilometers and 126 kilometers, respectively.
