item.title: S. Korea monitoring troop activities after N. Korean vessel marked 'coast guard' spotted near NLL
item.description: South Korea's military said Monday it is monitoring North Korean troop movements near the maritime border following a media report of a North Korean vessel marked "coast guard" spotted near the Northern Limit Line (NLL) in the Yellow Sea. Earlier in the day, a local newspaper reported the vessel marked "coast guard," the first North Korean ship seen bearing those words, was spotted last week near the de facto maritime border between the two Koreas. The vessel was equipped with what appeared to be 76-millimeter caliber naval artillery, the report said, noting it appeared to be monitoring Chinese fishing boats nearby. "Our military is closely monitoring and following the activities of North Korean forces," Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) spokesperson Capt. Jang Do-young told a press briefing. "The activities of North Korean vessels in the front-line maritime areas are under real-time monitoring of our military's surveillance systems," Jang said, without elaborating on the role and purpose of the spotted vessel. item.title: Lawmakers propose measures aimed at preventing covert filming using smart glasses
item.description: A group of lawmakers proposed on Monday a revision to rules aimed at mandating smart glasses to include functions that signal to others when photos are taken or videos are recorded, amid growing concerns of covert filming using such devices. The proposed amendment also aims to set guidelines so that users of smart glasses notify people nearby before taking a photo or recording a video. Violators could face fines of up to 10 million won ($7,424). "We plan to prepare guidelines to protect people's privacy from the recording phase, to prevent cases where people belatedly discover themselves being covertly filmed using smart glasses online," said ruling Democratic Party Rep. Lee Ju-hee, the lead sponsor of the bill. The move comes as concerns grow over smart glasses being used for spy cams and cheating at national or corporate exams. item.title: Son Yong-seok named Hankook Ilbo CEO
item.description: The Hankook Ilbo, the sister company of The Korea Times, said Monday that it has named Son Yong-seok, chief of its advertising business headquarters, as the paper’s new CEO and publisher. Son will begin his term on Dec. 1. Son is the first photojournalist to head a major Korean news outlet. A graduate of the Department of Korean Language and Literature at Chung-Ang University, Son joined the Hankook Ilbo in 1990. He later served as chief of the photo desk and head of the AD strategy headquarters. He also served as president of the Korea Press Photographers Association and currently chairs the Advertising Council of the Korea Newspaper Association. In a related reshuffle, Lee Tae-gyu, chief of the news content headquarters, will concurrently serve as editor. Park Il-keun, chief editorial writer, will lead the advertising business headquarters. Lee Sung-chul, who has served as CEO since December 2022, has been appointed an adviser.

item.title: Seoul Metropolitan Library to be renovated into multipurpose cultural space
item.description: The Seoul Metropolitan Library, housed in the former city hall, will be renovated into a multipurpose cultural space by 2029, city officials said Monday. The renovation project coincides with the 100th anniversary of the building's construction in 1926. A state-designated cultural heritage site, the building was converted into a public library in 2012. A public design competition will open Tuesday for the renovation of the library's four floors and an overhaul of its third-basement-floor archive, with the five floors spanning 7,556 square meters. To create a more spacious and open atmosphere, the city plans to relocate part of the library's current book collection from the upper floors to an underground storage area and install lower, more flexible bookshelves. The renovation will also add a kids' lounge for families and an open lecture hall for talks, educational programs and small gatherings. While the building's exterior and windows will be preserved in accordance with cultural heritage protection rules, the interior will be redesigned so citizens can freely spend time enjoying books

item.title: Immigration detainee denied video call with dying father, rights watchdog says
item.description: Korea's rights watchdog said Monday it recommended that an immigration detention center minimize restrictions on detainees' freedom of communication, after it found that a facility violated a detainee's right to pursue happiness by not allowing a video call with a dying father. The National Human Rights Commission of Korea, which made the recommendation last week, called on the center to guarantee that detainees can use their personal mobile phones to the extent necessary in urgent and serious humanitarian cases, such as when a family member is critically ill or dying. The complainant, a foreign national held at the center, brought the case to the commission in November 2025. The detainee claimed that they were refused after asking staff for permission to use a personal mobile phone to see their critically ill father one last time over a video call. The father died that day, and the complainant said the refusal deprived them of the most basic human right to pursue happiness. item.title: Seoul Arts Center emerges as premier global arts tourism destination
item.description: In southern Seoul’s Seocho District, a unique cultural corridor awaits travelers — one where grand Western symphonies meet the deep, resonant rhythms of traditional Korean music. Anchored by the Seoul Arts Center (SAC), the beating heart of Korea’s performing arts, and the neighboring National Gugak Center, the home of traditional Korean music, this district is rapidly positioning itself as a must-visit hub for international cultural tourists. On Thursday, the Seoul Tourism Organization (STO) held a backstage tour to showcase the area's potential as a high-end tourism product. Joined by inbound travel agencies from the Seoul Arts Tourism Alliance, foreign influencers from the Global Seoul Mates and members of the media, the tour explored how SAC and its surrounding landmarks can be woven into an immersive, stay-type arts itinerary. item.title: Bourse operator activates sell-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp fall
item.description: South Korea's bourse operator on Monday activated a sell-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the market came under heavy selling pressure. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes from 11:33 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). The measure was triggered for a second consecutive session. The KOSPI shed 248.96 points, or 5.11 percent to 4,211.00 as of 11:34 a.m. The KOSPI came under heavy downward pressure as investors tracked Wall Street losses amid concerns over the artificial intelligence (AI) sector. A sell-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index falls 5 percent or more for at least one minute.

item.title: GS25 expands into Cambodia with goal of 500 convenience stores
item.description: GS25 is taking its Korean convenience store formula to Cambodia, opening its first store in Phnom Penh and setting an ambitious target of more than 500 outlets in the country within 10 years. GS Retail, operator of the convenience store chain, said Monday it had signed a master franchise agreement with Cambodian company META Retail, expanding its overseas operations to three countries following Vietnam and Mongolia. The agreement followed more than a year of local market research and feasibility studies by the two companies. The first store, GS25 Olympic Stadium, opened Friday in the Cambodian capital, offering about 3,000 products, including the chain’s private-label brands Yours and Real Price. Korean products account for about 50 percent of its food selection, with offerings ranging from fish-shaped pastries known as "bungeoppang" and Korean snacks to ready-to-eat meals and triangular "gimbap." item.title: Judges' representative warns against DPK's push to impeach chief justice
item.description: A representative of judges nationwide has strongly criticized the ruling Democratic Party of Korea's push to impeach the Supreme Court chief justice, calling on his fellow judges to stand up against any attempt to undermine judicial independence. Kang Dong-won, a senior judge at the Seoul Family Court who also chairs the National Conference of Judge Representatives, issued the rebuke in a message posted on the court's internal network, CourtNet, on Sunday, accusing the DPK of "going beyond the bounds." The DPK announced its decision to seek the impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae after the top court on Thursday partially overturned an appellate ruling that sentenced former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo to 15 years in prison for playing a key role in former President Yoon Suk Yeol's failed martial law bid. The ruling party has since dropped Thursday's ruling from its list of impeachment grounds, instead citing the top court's alleged compliance with Yoon's martial law declaration, its decision to send President Lee Jae Myung's election law case back to the appeals court

item.title: Nat'l Assembly speaker to visit Japan, Australia to discuss parliamentary ties
item.description: National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik was set to embark on a seven-day trip to Japan and Australia on Monday to discuss ways to increase parliamentary cooperation, his office said. In Japan, Cho is scheduled to meet with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to discuss ways to expand parliamentary cooperation following the resumption of "shuttle diplomacy" between the countries' leaders, according to the office. He will also meet with Eisuke Mori, speaker of the House of Representatives, and House of Councilors President Masakazu Sekiguchi. item.title: Presidential office weighs extending restraining order against stalkers
item.description: The presidential office said Monday it is considering extending the period of restraining orders against stalkers as part of an initiative aimed at strengthening public safety and cracking down on crimes targeting vulnerable people. The initiative was announced by Cheong Wa Dae last week in response to growing public alarm over a series of relationship-based crimes and crimes with apparently random motives. The presidential office had said at the time that one of the measures under consideration was introducing life imprisonment without parole. "We will respond more strongly to crimes targeting the socially weak, including relationship-based crimes," presidential spokesperson Kim Sung-wan said at a press briefing, noting Wednesday will mark the start of the Week for the Elimination of Violence against Women, an annual government-designated campaign. item.title: New police chief vows to earn public trust in investigations
item.description: The new head of the National Police Agency (NPA) vowed Monday to make efforts to earn public trust in investigations as police take on a bigger role after the recent reform to the criminal justice system. NPA Commissioner General Kim Jong-chul made the pledge at his inauguration after Korea last month stripped prosecutors of their investigative powers, expanding the police role in criminal investigations. "Police will regard the criminal justice system reform as not an increase of authority but an expansion of grave responsibility," he said. "(I) will ensure the new criminal justice system is swiftly established and work to make police investigations more trusted." Kim, a former deputy NPA chief, fills the post that had been vacant for nearly two years since his predecessor was suspended from duty over his role in former President Yoon Suk Yeol's failed 2024 martial law bid. President Lee Jae Myung approved Kim's appointment Friday.

item.description: KG Mobility (KGM) is bringing one of its best-known SUV nameplates into the electrified era, unveiling the name and first teaser image of its next-generation flagship model, the Rexton plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV), ahead of its planned January 2027 launch. The automaker announced Monday that it had finalized the name of the vehicle, previously developed under the project code SE-10, combining its established Rexton brand with the PHEV designation. The new model will be KGM’s next-generation flagship SUV, equipped with a plug-in hybrid powertrain designed to extend the Rexton brand into electrified mobility while retaining its established identity. First introduced in 2001, the Rexton has represented KGM’s premium SUV lineup for 25 years, combining rugged styling and utility with the comfort and refinement traditionally associated with luxury sedans. item.title: Busan rallies global scientists in bid to host 2033 biochemistry congress
item.description: Busan is rallying leading life sciences researchers behind a bid to host a major international scientific congress in 2033, aiming to bring 5,000 specialists from about 80 countries to the southern port city. The Busan Metropolitan Government, Busan Tourism Organization, Inje University and the exhibition center BEXCO are teaming up with the Korean Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (KSBMB) to secure the hosting of the International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB) Congress. As part of the effort, KSBMB and Inje University will hold an international academic advisory appointment ceremony and commemorative symposium Tuesday at Ananti at Busan Cove in Gijang. Four prominent scientists will be appointed as international academic advisers, including Kaang Bong-kiun, Koh Gou-young, Narry Kim and Chun Jang-soo, will participate as international academic advisers. Their research has appeared in leading scientific journals, including Cell, Nature and Science. item.title: 'White Blast' tops box office in first weekend
item.description: The Korean film "White Blast" debuted at No. 1 at the local box office, attracting more than 300,000 moviegoers in its first weekend. The film garnered 310,000 admissions from Friday to Sunday, accounting for 39.6 percent of ticket sales at theaters nationwide, according to the Korean Film Council on Monday. Released Nov. 18, "White Blast" is a black comedy thriller set at a remote train station isolated by heavy snow. It follows retiring station master Gap-soo (Kim Yoon-seok) and his successor Hyun-taek (Koo Kyo-hwan) as they discover a body inside a railway tunnel while on patrol and grow suspicious of each other. It was co-directed by Hong Eui-jeong, known for "Voice of Silence" (2020), and newbie director Park Sun-woo. The Japanese animated film "Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island," which had held the No. 1 spot for six consecutive weeks through the previous weekend, fell to second place with around 91,000 admissions. item.title: YouTube, Sunfull urge Korean youth to pause before posting online
item.description: Students across Korea are being urged to pause before hitting "post" as a nationwide anti-cyberbullying campaign expands to tackle artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content, organizers said Monday. The Sunfull Foundation and YouTube launched the Just a Moment campaign during a joint declaration ceremony at the National Assembly in Seoul on Friday, where they also recognized top contributors and outlined their 2026 initiatives. The event was co-hosted by the foundation and Rep. Kang Kyung-sook, with support from YouTube. Now in its third year, the campaign encourages internet users to pause for a few seconds and reconsider before sharing posts or leaving comments. This year, organizers expanded its digital literacy education beyond combating malicious comments to include helping young people distinguish AI-generated content. Students in classrooms nationwide watched campaign videos featuring actress Hye-ri and EBS character Pengsoo, joining in the message: “Pause for just a moment before you press the button!” The foundation also partnered with YouTube on in-person digital literacy

item.title: Sejong University study sheds light on role of cell death in plant immunity
item.description: A Sejong University research team has published a collaborative international study shedding new light on how plants use a form of cell death to fight infections and how the rice blast fungus uses a similar process to infect plants. The study, published in the international journal iMeta, was led by Jwa Nam-soo, a professor in the university’s Department of Integrative Bioscience and Biotechnology. Researcher Nam Khoa Nguyen was listed as a co-first author, while Jwa was a co-corresponding author. The paper, titled “Decoding ferroptosis via integrated multi-omics analyses in rice blast,” examines ferroptosis, a form of regulated cell death caused by iron-dependent oxidation of lipids, or fats, in cell membranes. Using integrated multi-omics analyses, the researchers identified contrasting roles of ferroptosis in plant immune responses and in the rice blast fungus’s infection process. They also proposed a model linking iron metabolism, reactive oxygen species, lipid oxidation and calcium signaling. The study builds on Jwa’s long-standing research into plant immune-related cell de

item.title: Personal information of more than 8,000 clients at Samsung Securities breached
item.description: Personal data belonging to over 8,000 clients of Samsung Securities has been breached, the brokerage said Monday, in the latest cyberattack against Korean financial firms. Samsung Securities said unauthorized access was detected on its customer response website last Saturday and the data breach did not affect other customer information beyond the affected system. Customer names, physical addresses and other personal information were compromised, Samsung Securities said. The brokerage said it reported the incident to the relevant authorities, who have been scrambling to deal with data breaches in recent months. The firm then said it has moved to strengthen its cybersecurity systems.

item.title: LS Cable secures record $500 mil. US export deal
item.description: LS Cable & System has secured a 700 billion won ($500 million) order to supply and install high-voltage cables for a major power grid project in New York, marking the largest U.S. export project ever won by a Korean cablemaker. The company said Monday that its U.S. subsidiary, LS Cable Systems America, will supply and install 345-kilovolt (kV) extra-high-voltage underground and submarine cable systems for the Propel NY Energy project. The project, jointly developed by the New York Power Authority (NYPA) and transmission developer New York Transco, involves building an approximately 145-kilometer (90-mile) transmission network linking Long Island with Queens and the Bronx in New York City, as well as Westchester County. It aims to expand transmission capacity, improve grid reliability and facilitate the integration of renewable energy sources, including offshore wind power. The project moved closer to construction after the New York State Public Service Commission approved construction plans for its first and second phases on Thursday. item.title: Korea asks Qatar to prioritize LNG supplies once production, shipping normalize
item.description: Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan on Monday requested that Qatar give priority to supplying liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Korea when Qatari LNG production and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz return to normal, the ministry said. During a meeting with Qatari Minister of State for Energy Affairs Saad Sherida al-Kaabi in Seoul, Kim stressed that the Middle Eastern country is a key partner for Korea in the LNG sector and that cooperation between the two countries is crucial to ensuring a stable energy supply, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. He asked Qatar to prioritize Korea in LNG supplies once conditions return to normal. item.title: Zerobaseone to release new album in January
item.description: K-pop boy group Zerobaseone will return with a new album on Jan. 18, 2027. The group revealed the release date at the end of its performance at the 2026 MAMA Awards in Osaka, Japan, on Saturday, displaying a sign reading "Jan. 18, 2027." The upcoming release will be Zerobaseone's first full-group album in eight months, following its sixth EP, "Ascend-," released in May. The album's title and tracklist have not yet been disclosed. Zerobaseone, now a five-member group, has balanced group activities with unit and solo projects both at home and in Japan this year.

item.title: Lawyer: Father and daughter detained by ICE at Seattle airport were traveling to family baptism
item.description: A father and daughter detained by masked immigration officers on an airport jet bridge in Seattle , causing chaos in front of other passengers, were heading to a family baptism ceremony in California, their lawyer said Sunday. Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday used their cellphones to film the father and daughter being detained by the officers, who were wearing unmarked jackets and khaki pants. The recordings were widely viewed on social media. The videos show the officers struggling with someone on the ground. The flight, bound for Los Angeles, was delayed. The father and daughter were traveling to attend a baptism ceremony in California and are seeking asylum in the U.S., where they have lived since 2015, their lawyer, Olia Catala, told The Associated Press in a telephone interview. item.title: Exports more than double in 1st 20 days of November, with chip shipments surging to new high
item.description: Korea's exports more than doubled during the first 20 days of November, with shipments of semiconductors surging to a record high, customs data showed Monday. Outbound shipments reached $77.4 billion in the Nov. 1-20 period, up from $38.4 billion a year ago, according to the data from the Korea Customs Service. It marked the highest figure for the first 20 days of any month. The daily average export value in terms of business days also reached $4.84 billion, the highest for the first 20 days of any month. The combined exports from Jan. 1 through Friday came to $1.01 trillion, up 63.2 percent from a year earlier. Imports also jumped 39.4 percent on-year to $50.3 billion over the cited period, resulting in a trade surplus of $27.1 billion. By sector, exports of chips nearly quadrupled to $38.5 billion, setting a fresh record for the 20-day period. As a result, chip exports accounted for 49.7 percent of the country's total outbound shipment, a sharp increase of 24.3 percentage points from a year earlier. item.title: Seoul shares extend losses late Monday morning on AI-driven tech sell-off
item.description: South Korean shares extended their losses late Monday morning as a global technology rout intensified, with foreign investors turning net sellers and offloading major chip shares. After opening 2.77 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) fell 210.63 points, or 4.33 percent, to 4,659.33 as of 11:20 a.m. Foreign investors, who had been net buyers early in the session, shifted to net selling, further adding to downward pressure on the index. On Friday (local time), U.S. stocks tumbled amid intensified concerns over heavy investments by big tech firms in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. In Seoul, chip stocks led the decline. Market bellwether Samsung Electronics fell 4.72 percent, while its chipmaking rival SK hynix declined 4.13 percent. Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution slid 3.26 percent, and pharmaceutical giant Samsung Biologics fell 5.61 percent. The Korean won was quoted at 1,346.5 won against the U.S. dollar as of 11:20 a.m., up 0.5 won from the previous session's close.

item.title: Lee's approval rating rises for 2nd straight week to 37.3%: poll
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating rose for the second consecutive week last week to 37.3 percent, a poll showed Monday. In a poll conducted on 2,514 adults nationwide from last Monday to Friday by Realmeter, positive assessments of Lee's job performance rose by 0.9 percentage point from the previous week, while negative assessments fell 1 percentage point to 59.9 percent. Realmeter attributed the rise in Lee's approval rating to diplomatic and economic achievements, including his attendance at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summits in the Philippines and China, respectively, as well as his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit. The pollster also cited South Korea's exports topping the US$1 trillion mark as a positive factor but said domestic concerns, such as the KOSPI stock market index falling below 5,000 points and the recent controversy over artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating on the college entrance exam, held back further gains in his approval rating. item.title: Mark to release new studio album next month
item.description: Singer Mark will release his new studio album "Windmill" on Dec. 4, his agency Upper Room said Monday. The album will feature 12 tracks, including the lead track, "'What's Your Dream?,' 'Don't Have One,'" as well as "Brian," "Happiest," "Never Dies," "My Friend," "Home," "Ready or Not" and "Your Day." The lead track's unusual name reflects its format of answering the question "What is your dream?" with "I don't have one," the agency said. Mark, also known as Mark Lee, prereleased "My Friend" and "Happiest."

item.title: N. Korea's Kim says Pyongyang seeks no regional dominance, defending arms buildup as self-defense
item.description: North Korea does not seek regional dominance or expansion, leader Kim Jong-un has said, defending its military buildup as the exercise of its sovereign right, state media reported Monday. Kim made the remarks at a ceremony Sunday, where he received credentials from newly appointed ambassadors from Russia, Sweden, Indonesia, Vietnam, Brazil, the Czech Republic, India, the Philippines, Thailand and Bangladesh, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). He described a world growing more unstable and unpredictable, one in which some countries put their own interests above international law and trample the sovereignty of others. "The security situation in the DPRK and the political and military environment in East Asia urgently demand that we provide for ourselves the power and capability with which we can be fully ensured of security and confidence in peace," he said, defending Pyongyang's drive to expand its arsenal. item.title: Ateez scores 4th No. 1 on Billboard 200 with 'Golden Hour: Part. 6'
item.description: K-pop boy group Ateez has claimed its fourth No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard's main albums chart with its new album, "Golden Hour: Part. 6." Billboard reported in a chart preview Sunday (local time) that "Golden Hour: Part. 6" secured the top spot this week over albums from big-name stars, such as Olivia Rodrigo and Morgan Wallen. It marks the group's fourth No. 1 on the chart, following "The World Ep. Final: Will" in 2023, "Golden Hour: Part. 2" in 2024 and "Golden Hour: Part. 5" in July of this year. Including the latest release, Ateez has logged 10 consecutive albums on the Billboard 200. With 10 top-10 entries in the 2020s, it now has the most top 10s among groups this decade. Team leader Hongjoong said through the group's agency, KQ Entertainment, that he was "overwhelmed and grateful" to have earned the group's fourth No. 1 on the Billboard 200, crediting Atiny, the group's fandom, for the feat. item.title: US seeks answers on Nvidia's sale of chips to China, Bessent says
item.description: WASHINGTON — The US is seeking answers from Nvidia on its chip sales to China and will find out who was in charge of compliance at the company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday. "We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers.... It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was," Bessent told the CBS program "Face the Nation." Reports about Huang's relationship with a woman whom US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy and his extramarital affair with a company executive led to his resignation and investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit. item.title: Russia starts towing ship hit by drones in Baltic, Finland says
item.description: HELSINKI — A Russian rescue vessel on Sunday began towing a Russian-owned cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea out of Finnish waters after two days of firefighting, Finland's coast guard said. The Finnish military has said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was likely carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters. The 16 crew members were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship. One crew member was slightly injured. "Thermal cameras show that some containers are warm, but the vessel is stable enough for towing to begin," Finland's coast guard said in a statement. It said that responsibility for the rescue will transfer to Russia once the ship leaves Finnish waters. Pictures and video released earlier by the Finnish coast guard showed several vessels spraying the Sparta II with water cannons during the night in a bid to put out the flames and cool down containers stacked on its deck. item.title: Can climate diplomacy build on collapse of COP31?
item.description: ANTALYA, Turkey — The collapse of COP31 talks in Turkey on Sunday without a political agreement left exhausted negotiators questioning the future of a process that for three decades has led the global fight against climate change. For the small, vulnerable countries most exposed to rising sea levels and the increasingly extreme weather scientists link to rising carbon emissions, annual UN conferences are their chance to draw the world's attention to their plight and seek financial help. But the failure of the Turkish talks, which follows on from weak outcomes at other COPs in recent years, lays bare the need for change. Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, director of environment in Peru's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said "the credibility of the process" was at stake. "This system needs in-depth reforms," he said. Simon Stiell, the UN climate chief representing the UN convention that underpins international climate talks, said the consensus-based system can still function, but work was needed. "I have taken steps in engaging external knowledge leaders in advising on areas of potential reform.

item.title: Like SpaceX, Anthropic ran an unusual IPO process, chafing some bankers
item.description: NEW YORK — For the second time this year, Wall Street bankers and lawyers took home a massive paycheck from a record-setting initial public offering. And for the second time this year, some of them came out of it complaining in private about how the process was riddled with complications and unlike any they had worked on before. With SpaceX’s IPO in June, in which banks earned half a billion dollars in fees, bankers chafed over how tightly the Elon Musk-led company controlled the months-long process and kept financial and other information private, making it hard for advisers to do their jobs. item.title: 'The Remarried Empress' shows IP synergy as Disney+ hit lifts webtoon views
item.description: Global views for the webtoon "The Remarried Empress" surged 35-fold following the premiere of its Disney+ drama adaptation, highlighting the growing synergy between Korean web content and global streaming platforms. During the two weeks from Nov. 3 to 16, global views for the original webtoon jumped about 35 times compared to the two-week period from Aug. 12 to 25, right before the drama's teaser trailer was released, Naver Webtoon, a digital comics platform operated by Webtoon Entertainment, said Sunday. Viewership increased across all available languages, with Korean-language views soaring 54-fold and English-language views climbing 35-fold. Naver added that downloads and views for the original web novel on Naver Series jumped roughly 45-fold during the same period. Set in a fictional Western country, the romance fantasy follows Navier (Shin Min-a), the empress of the Eastern Empire, who agrees to a divorce demanded by Emperor Sovieshu (Ju Ji-hoon) on the condition that she can remarry Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk), a prince from the neighboring Western Kingdom. item.title: ALL'N wants violin to be hook, not gimmick, in K-pop
item.description: Strings are no strangers to K-pop, usually brought in to lend drama to a track's intro or swell beneath its bridge. Singer-violinist ALL'N, however, asks the instrument to do something harder and more important — carry most of a song's hook. On "Four Seasons," the title track of his first mini album of the same name, out Monday, the violin opens the song, answers the chorus and takes over the final post-chorus, doing the work a vocal hook usually would. "It's easy to add a violin section that sounds impressive, but I want a hook that someone remembers and wants to hear again," the 32-year-old told The Korea Times in a written interview. For the classically trained violinist, who also writes, produces and runs his own agency, the album caps a debut year spent testing how far the instrument can go inside a pop song. "I didn't want the violin to be something I brought out briefly to surprise people," he said. "I wanted it to be part of how they recognized my music." item.title: Peugeot moves car shopping to Naver
item.description: Peugeot is moving more of the car-buying journey online by offering vehicle reservations and test-drive bookings through its official Naver store, allowing customers to compare prices and specifications without switching between platforms. The auto brand under Stellantis Korea opened its official store on Naver in October, enabling customers to make purchase reservations for all models sold in Korea. Naver is the nation’s dominant internet portal. In November, the automaker added a test-drive booking function, so customers move from browsing to arranging a test drive without leaving the platform. Previously, customers who wanted to test-drive a vehicle after viewing it on Peugeot’s online store had to use the automaker’s official website. Now, they can check prices and specifications on a model page and use the same Naver account to book a test drive or make a purchase reservation. The move comes as online commerce continues to expand in Korea, including the automotive sector. item.title: N. Korean leader receives credentials from Russian ambassador in protocol shift after 30 years
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un received credentials from Russia's new ambassador to Pyongyang on Sunday, marking the first time in more than 30 years that the country's top leader has directly received credentials from a foreign envoy, reports said. The Russian Embassy in Pyongyang said on its Telegram channel that Ambassador Andrei Podelyshev presented his credentials to Kim earlier in the day. Kim also received credentials from diplomats of several other countries, shaking hands with them and delivering a speech, according to the Russia's Tass news agency. The move follows a constitutional revision in March that granted the chairman of the State Affairs Commission, a post held by Kim, the authority to receive credentials from foreign diplomats. Under the previous system, the chairman of the Standing Committee of the Supreme People's Assembly (SPA) performed the role. Kim's grandfather and national founder Kim Il-sung personally received credentials from foreign ambassadors, while the SPA Standing Committee chairman did so under his father, Kim Jong-il. item.title: Miley Cyrus weds drummer Maxx Morando
item.description: Grammy-winning pop star Miley Cyrus married her longtime partner, drummer Maxx Morando, in California on Saturday, People magazine and other U.S. entertainment news outlets reported. Cyrus and Morando reportedly tied the knot at a private ceremony in Palm Springs, a month after performing "Let's Get Married" together at the Hollywood Bowl. The song appears on Cyrus' latest studio album, Bass Persuades. Representatives for both Cyrus and Morando did not immediately respond to a Reuters' request for comment. Morando is the drummer for Liily, a Los Angeles-based alternative rock band affiliated with Atlantic Records, according to the band's website. The "Flowers" singer was previously married to Australian actor Liam Hemsworth, who filed for divorce in Los Angeles in 2019.

item.title: KEPCO reports another massive data breach
item.description: The state-run Korea Electric Power (KEPCO) said Sunday it has confirmed another data breach involving the personal information of around 1.52 million users, a month after disclosing a separate leak affecting tens of thousands of people. The power utility said personal information belonging to 650,487 users of its KEPCO ON customer service platform and 869,761 users of its electronic procurement system, known as SRM, had been leaked. The KEPCO ON breach exposed customers' names, resident registration numbers, bank account details, credit card information, and electricity rates and billing records, while the SRM breach exposed information on 426,827 corporate representatives, including their names, phone numbers and email addresses. The SRM breach exposed personal information of 426,827 corporate representatives, including their names, registration numbers and email addresses, as well as 442,934 KEPCO and company employees, whose names, affiliations and contact details were leaked. item.title: Rail union postpones threatened labor action following train derailment
item.description: The Korean Railway Workers' Union said Sunday it has postponed its planned work-to-rule action to later this week to prioritize the restoration of train services following a recent freight train derailment. The union had planned to launch the work-to-rule action at 9 a.m. Monday, with workers strictly following work rules to demand more maintenance and station staff, and expanded facilities for high-speed train maintenance and storage. But it decided to postpone the labor action by three days to Thursday, after a freight train derailed at Sojeong-ri Station on the Gyeongbu Line in Sejong on Saturday morning, disrupting train services in the area. "We will postpone the work-to-rule action until rail services are stabilized and do our best to support the recovery effort," the union said, adding it would call for measures to prevent a recurrence once the cause of the accident is identified. No casualties were reported, but power outages and track obstructions disrupted services, leading to the suspension of regular passenger trains on the line Saturday. Train services had returned to normal

item.title: N. Korea to hold int'l Pyongyang marathon in Oct. 2027: tour agency
item.description: North Korea plans to hold an international marathon in its capital of Pyongyang in October next year, a tour agency that is an official partner of the event said Sunday. Koryo Tours, a Beijing-based tour agency specializing in North Korea, said in a social media post that the 2027 Pyongyang International Marathon would take place in October, adding that the exact date would be announced once officially confirmed. If held as planned, the event would mark a shift from its traditional schedule in April to October. North Korea has held the international marathon in Pyongyang since 1981 to mark the April 15 birthday of late national founder, Kim Il-sung. The marathon was not held for five consecutive years from 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic before resuming in 2025. But this year's event was abruptly canceled by North Korean authorities about a month before the scheduled date, though it had planned to hold the race on April 5 and promoted tour packages through Koryo Tours to recruit foreign participants.

item.title: Coast Guard finds hull of missing fishing boat Haegwangho on seabed
item.description: The Coast Guard said Sunday it confirmed that an object found on the seabed off Korea's west coast was the hull of the missing fishing boat Haegwangho, as the search entered its fifth day. The Coast Guard had been working to identify the object it had earlier discovered lying on the seabed near where the Haegwangho went missing off the western coastal county of Taean last Wednesday. Coast Guard officials confirmed that what had appeared to be a sunken ship was the missing boat. The Haegwangho, a 7.93-ton boat carrying three Koreans and four Indonesians, was reported missing early last Wednesday. It had left a port in Taean two days earlier.

item.title: Sungkyunkwan University forum explores advances in next-generation solar cells
item.description: Sungkyunkwan University hosted the 14th Sungkyun International Solar Forum at its Seoul campus from Nov. 11-13, bringing together researchers to discuss advances in perovskite solar cells and optoelectronic devices. The forum came amid growing demand for carbon-free energy sources to address the climate crisis, as electricity demand continues to rise due to the expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers and the increasing adoption of electric vehicles. Commercializing perovskite solar cells, which are seen as a next-generation power generation technology, and developing technologies for mass production have emerged as key challenges. Park Nam-gyu, a distinguished professor of chemical engineering at the university and director of the SKKU National Laboratory for Intelligent Energy Solution Technology, chaired the forum’s organizing committee. He presented the latest research findings on perovskite solar cells and outlined technological developments aimed at their commercialization. The university said Park was the first researcher in the world to develop solid-state perovski

item.title: Ruling party outlines grounds to impeach chief justice
item.description: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) laid out its grounds Sunday for impeaching Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae and said it would seek a National Assembly vote by the end of December, drawing criticism that the move could undermine judicial independence. At its first public briefing at the Assembly, the party’s impeachment task force pointed to the Supreme Court’s handling of President Lee Jae Myung’s election law case and Cho’s refusal to recommend a new candidate for a vacant Supreme Court seat. “We will do our utmost to finalize the impeachment motion as quickly as possible and bring it to a vote in the National Assembly before the end of December,” said Rep. Yang Bu-nam, who leads the task force. He did not give a date for filing the motion. Other grounds previously raised by the party include the court’s response to the Dec. 3, 2024, martial law declaration, allegations over court operating expenses and cash payments, and Cho’s refusal to testify before the Assembly. item.title: Half of Korean workers fear workplace photos could be used in AI sex crimes
item.description: More than half of workers in Korea worry that photos of themselves posted on company intranets or messaging platforms could be used in artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted sex crimes, a survey showed Sunday. According to the survey commissioned by labor rights group Workplace Gapjil 119 and conducted by polling firm Global Research, 53.1 percent of 1,000 workers aged 19 or older said they were concerned that their workplace photos could be exploited for such crimes. The survey was conducted from Aug. 1–7. The concern was more widespread among women, with 58.2 percent expressing anxiety, compared with 49 percent among male respondents. The survey also pointed to a lack of safeguards at companies. Only 11.6 percent of respondents said their employers had rules in place to prevent and respond to AI-related sex crimes. Nearly half, or 48.6 percent, said their companies had no such rules, while another 39.8 percent said they did not know whether such rules existed. item.title: Korean consortium wins Vietnam high-speed rail design contract
item.description: The Korea National Railway and two Korean engineering firms will take part in a project to develop a high-speed railway connecting northern and southern Vietnam, spanning 1,541 kilometers between Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, according to Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Sunday. A consortium comprising Korean, French and Vietnamese companies has won a contract for a feasibility study and front-end engineering design (FEED) for the project. The contract was tendered by the Thang Long Project Management Unit under Vietnam's Ministry of Construction. The consortium includes state-run Korea National Railway and Korean engineering firms Yooshin and Sambo, along with France's Systra and Vietnam's Tedi, both of which specialize in railway design. The consortium won the contract in competition with 40 other bidders, according to the ministry. The initial phase of the project is valued at 560 billion won ($416 million), with the consortium set to carry out the work over 30 months. item.title: [COVER STORY] 'AI spending binge puts Samsung, SK at risk of memory price collapse'
item.description: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix could face a sharp memory price decline if hyperscalers scale back the artificial intelligence (AI) spending that has driven the current chip boom, according to a renowned U.S. semiconductor analyst. Jim Handy, founder and general director at Objective Analysis, said in an interview with The Korea Times that the surge in memory prices — caused by a sharp increase in demand — is “temporary,” echoing concerns among some Korean analysts that the current memory cycle may be nearing its peak. “I do not think that AI demand is growing that quickly, so they are likely to slow their spending at some point, and that will cause memory prices to collapse,” Handy said. Although the timing of a downturn is difficult to predict, memory prices could eventually fall back to 2024 levels once demand weakens, he said. Handy has raised particular concerns over the scale of spending by hyperscalers such as Google, Meta, Amazon and OpenAI. item.title: KOSPI rout fuels calls for bolder stabilization measures
item.description: Calls are growing for the government to take stronger steps to stabilize the stock market after KOSPI fell to a 10-month low, with market watchers and lawmakers warning Sunday that further losses could follow. The benchmark index closed at 4,869.96 on Friday, down 267.93 points, or 5.21 percent, from the previous session. It marked its first close below 4,900 in about 10 months. The index lost 7.95 percent over the week as growing doubts over the returns on artificial intelligence investments weighed on major semiconductor stocks. The steep decline has put the financial authorities' response under scrutiny, with critics saying measures introduced so far have done little to calm the market. Jung Jeom-sik, floor leader of the main opposition People Power Party, urged the government to prepare emergency measures for a possible "Black Monday," warning that the market could face an even sharper fall. item.title: Korea holds landmark Kimchi Day vision declaration in New York
item.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs said Sunday that it held its first-ever Kimchi Global Vision Declaration ceremony in New York on Friday (local time) to mark the seventh annual Kimchi Day and promote kimchi in global markets. Kimchi Day was first designated on Nov. 22, 2020 to honor kimchi's cultural heritage, ingredients and health benefits. The event, held at the Korean Cultural Center New York, brought together about 100 participants, including New York State Assemblymember Ron Kim, Korean Consul General in New York Kim Sang-ho, chef Hooni Kim and local food industry representatives. During the event, Jeong Gyeong-seok, director general of the ministry's Food Industry Policy Bureau, outlined four priorities: studying kimchi's potential benefits for gut health and immunity; using artificial intelligence to automate production and improve quality control; preserving more than 200 regional and seasonal varieties while expanding education; and working with retailers and restaurants to expand offerings, including vegan kimchi. item.title: Kookmin University teams up with QNX to introduce Korea's first embedded software curriculum
item.description: Kookmin University established the QNX Centre Korea on Nov. 4 in partnership with QNX, a global provider of embedded software and operating systems, to provide specialized education in the field. The university said the center will serve as a platform for industry-academia collaboration aimed at nurturing talent in embedded software. Through the partnership, Kookmin University becomes the first university in Korea to introduce a curriculum based on QNX technology. QNX, a division of BlackBerry Limited, provides operating systems and software development technologies for industries where safety and reliability are critical, including the automotive, medical device and industrial automation sectors. The university plans to develop the center into a hub for embedded software education and industry-academia cooperation, connecting academic institutions, government agencies and industry partners across Korea. The initiative aims to cultivate skilled professionals in various fields, including software-defined vehicles, robotics, industrial automation, smart factories and the industrial internet

item.title: Ramyeon exports set to approach $2 bil. this year on global popularity
item.description: Exports of "ramyeon," or instant noodles, are set to approach $2 billion this year amid the expanding global popularity of Korean food and culture, industry data showed Sunday. Ramyeon shipments rose 26.3 percent to $1.59 billion in the January-October period, already surpassing last year's full-year total of $1.52 billion, according to data from the Korea Agro-Fisheries & Food Trade Corp. If the growth trend continues through the rest of the year, annual ramyeon exports are expected to approach $2 billion. Korea's ramyeon exports have steadily increased since 2014. China was the biggest buyer, importing $395.5 million worth in the 10-month period, up 23.9 percent from a year earlier. Exports to the United States rose 29.1 percent to $276.5 million over the cited period. Exports to Europe and Central and South America also posted strong growth. Ramyeon shipments to the Netherlands soared 41.3 percent to $95.7 million, while those to Britain rose 41.9 percent to $60.4 million. Exports to Mexico surged 190.4 percent to $51.9 million.

item.title: Education minister resigns amid backlash over CSAT anti-cheating measures
item.description: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin offered to resign Sunday, taking responsibility for confusion over anti-cheating measures in the run-up to the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). President Lee Jae Myung accepted his resignation within an hour. "Last-minute changes in preparations for the CSAT caused inconvenience to the public, particularly test takers," Choi said in a statement released by the ministry. With the exam now over, Choi acknowledged responsibility for the confusion and announced his decision to step down. The resignation followed mounting criticism of the ministry's slow response to concerns over artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating ahead of the CSAT, Korea's high-stakes college entrance exam. The government repeatedly revised its anti-cheating measures just days before the test, leaving students and test administrators scrambling to keep up with the changes. item.title: Sejong University medical device startup secures $9.7 mil. in new investments
item.description: Raywatt, a medical device startup founded by a Sejong University professor, has raised 13 billion won ($9.7 million) in a new funding round, bringing its cumulative funding to more than 23.5 billion won. Ha Jin-yong, a professor in the university’s Department of AI Convergence Electronics Engineering, launched the company in 2019. It specializes in medical imaging devices for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diagnosis. The investors included participation from InterVest, Life Asset Management, Ryukyung PSG Asset Management, Hyundai Venture Investment, L&S Venture Capital, Eugene Investment & Securities and EcoPro Partners. Investors recognized Raywatt’s achievements in commercializing its technology both in Korea and overseas. The company’s technology has been used in more than 100 clinical cases at Severance Cardiovascular Hospital in Seoul. It has also been designated an innovative prototype product by the Public Procurement Service. item.title: Trump again calls Putin 'friend' despite criticism in US
item.description: Washington — US President Donald Trump again called Russian President Vladimir Putin his "friend" on Saturday, despite fierce criticism from US lawmakers. Trump posted a photo on Truth Social showing the two leaders shaking hands, accompanied by the caption "My Friend." The post followed a summit in China this week, where Trump greeted Putin warmly and referred to him as a friend, drawing criticism from Democrats and some Republicans. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer accused Putin of abducting tens of thousands of children, killing tens of thousands of civilians and wrongfully detaining US citizens. "Donald Trump considers him a friend," Schumer wrote on X. Republican Senator Rick Scott of Florida described Putin as a "thug." Ahead of the summit, Republican Senator Jim Banks of Indiana also warned that China and Russia were "not our friends," calling for a tough stance toward both countries. At a White House press conference on Friday, Trump again praised his ties with Putin, despite Russia's nearly five-year war against Ukraine. "I have fantastic relationships with Putin," he said. H

item.title: Coast Guard finds vessel-like object on seabed amid search for missing fishing boat
item.description: The Coast Guard said Sunday it has located an object believed to be a sunken vessel on the seabed near where a fishing boat went missing off South Korea's west coast last week. The unidentified object was detected by naval sonar at 7:55 p.m. Saturday, according to the Taean Coast Guard. The object lies 52 meters deep and roughly 41 kilometers northwest of an island off Taean, about 110 km southwest of Seoul. The location is near the site where the fishing boat Haegwangho went missing Wednesday. Officials said they are working to determine whether the object is linked to the vessel. The search entered its fifth day Sunday for the seven crew members who remain missing, as well as the 7.93-ton boat. High waves and strong winds have hampered search and rescue operations. The Navy said it is sending its 3,500-ton Tongyeong rescue and salvage ship to the site to carry out a detailed underwater search. The Navy will also deploy an unmanned remotely operated vehicle (ROV) from the salvage ship to help identify the object found on the seabed. An ROV is connected to a mothership and used to explore

item.description: Hana Financial Group said Sunday that it provided winter supplies and home safety equipment to senior citizens from vulnerable communities as part of efforts to improve their living conditions and prevent household accidents. item.title: Van Gogh Museum bistro drops kimchi sandwich after 'Japanese' labeling controversy
item.description: A restaurant inside the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam has changed its menu after it faced criticism for listing a sandwich with kimchi on a menu that cited Japanese but not Korean influences on the cuisine served. Seo Kyoung-duk, a professor at Sungshin Women’s University and an advocate for Korean culture, said Sunday that a recent visitor to the Van Gogh Museum found the kimchi sandwich missing from Bistro Vincent’s menu. The item had been replaced with a new item described as including Japanese milk bread. The change comes about six months after the controversy first emerged in May. Sunday was also Kimchi Day in Korea, observed annually on Nov. 22. Bistro Vincent describes its cuisine as French food with a Japanese twist, made with Dutch ingredients. Listing a kimchi sandwich on its menu raised concerns that the Korean fermented dish could be mistaken for Japanese food. While welcoming the change, Seo expressed apprehension that similar cases remain widespread across the continent. “This kind of incident is still happening frequently in Europe, which is concerning,” he said. This

item.title: Korea's car trade deficit with China hits record on Tesla EV imports
item.description: South Korea's deficit in the car trade with China rose to a record high in the January-October period on rising demand for Tesla electric vehicles (EVs) made in China, industry data showed Sunday. South Korea exported $168.77 million worth of cars to China in the first 10 months of the year, down 34.9 percent from the same period last year, according to data from the Korea International Trade Association (KITA) and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. However, its imports of cars from China surged 79.2 percent on-year to $4.39 billion over the cited period, bringing the trade deficit to a record $4.23 billion. South Korea has recorded a deficit in the car trade with China every year since 2017, with the gap widening sharply from $466 million in 2022 to $943 million in 2023 and $1.73 billion in 2024. The widening deficit is largely attributed to strong sales of Tesla EVs manufactured at the U.S. automaker's Gigafactory in Shanghai. item.title: Korea expected to become world's 4th-largest exporter this year
item.description: South Korea is expected to rank fourth globally in annual exports this year after its cumulative exports surpassed $1 trillion for the first time last week, data showed Sunday. According to data from the World Trade Organization (WTO) and U.N. Comtrade, a trade statistics database run by the United Nations, South Korea posted $595.3 billion in exports in the first seven months of 2026. It ranked fifth, behind China with $2.52 trillion, the United States with $1.44 trillion, Germany with $1.12 trillion and the Netherlands with $627.7 billion. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said it believes South Korea overtook the Netherlands after July as exports accelerated, driven by strong semiconductor shipments amid an artificial intelligence (AI) boom. The ministry said South Korea is expected to finish the year as the world's fourth-largest exporter, with annual shipments reaching $1.17 trillion. item.title: SK chair urges Korea-Japan joint AI talent development program
item.description: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has called for a fundamental overhaul of education to prepare for an artificial intelligence (AI)-native society, urging Korean and Japanese universities and businesses to jointly develop talent for the AI era. Chey made the remarks at Tokyo Forum 2026 on Saturday, emphasizing the need to redesign education systems for a society in which AI is accepted as an integral part of everyday life rather than simply used as a tool. The two-day forum, co-hosted by the Chey Institute for Advanced Studies and the University of Tokyo, started Friday under the theme "AI as a Transformative Technology: Humanity, Knowledge and Civilization." It brought together global experts, including French government AI envoy Anne Bouverot and Sakana AI co-founder Ren Ito. item.title: Samsung Electronics, SK hynix dividend payout ratios surge through Q3 amid AI boom
item.description: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix saw their dividend payout ratios rise sharply through the third quarter under their shareholder return policies, data showed Sunday, amid the memory chip boom driven by artificial intelligence (AI). According to the companies' respective quarterly reports, Samsung Electronics' dividend payout ratio stood at 18 percent on a consolidated basis as of end-September, up from 4.1 percent at the end of the first half, while SK hynix's ratio rose to 8.4 percent from 0.4 percent over the same period. A dividend payout ratio refers to the proportion of a company's earnings distributed to shareholders as dividends, serving as an indicator of how a company allocates its profits. The sharp increases came as the two chipmakers announced plans to distribute sizable dividends to shareholders as part of their respective shareholder return policies. Samsung Electronics decided to pay 30 trillion won ($22.3 billion) in dividends for the third quarter, or 4,601 won per share, compared with 372 won per common share in the first quarter and 374 won in the second quarter. item.title: Virginia reports young child is the state's first measles death in 2026
item.description: A young child has died in Virginia after testing positive for measles, officials said, the first deadly case in the state this year. The Virginia Department of Health reported the death Friday, saying only that the child was under 5 years old. Just days earlier the U.S., along with Mexico and Bolivia, lost its designation as having eliminated the highly contagious virus. States have reported at least 12 measles-linked deaths in 2026. Eight of them, including one last week, have been in Pennsylvania, one was in New York and two were in Wisconsin. Virginia has reported 220 cases overall this year, most of them in the central part of the state, and the vast majority were among people not vaccinated against the virus. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has tracked more than 5,800 cases nationally in 2026, by far the most of any year since 1991. item.title: Mexico captures top drug lord 'El Chapo Isidro,' latest in string of arrests
item.description: MEXICO CITY — Mexican military forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, and two other leaders of his drug-trafficking organization in Sinaloa state on Friday night, Mexico's security chief said on Saturday. For over 20 years, according to the US State Department, Meza Flores and his criminal organization smuggled vast amounts of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine and marijuana into the United States. He was considered one of the leaders of the Beltran Leyva cartel, previously a rival of the Sinaloa cartel. After Sinaloa cartel founder Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada was taken into US custody in 2024, infighting began between two factions for control of the cartel, Los Chapitos and Los Mayos. Meza Flores' Beltran Leyva had recently allied with the Los Mayos faction, security experts say. The arrest is the latest in a string of captures and killings of high-profile suspected drug traffickers by Mexico, which is under pressure from US President Donald Trump. item.title: Climate talks in overtime as nations wrestle with response to worsening global warming
item.description: ANTALYA, Turkey — Work crews boxed up the venue for this year’s United Nations climate talks in Turkey, as negotiators went into overtime on Saturday in an attempt to reach a final agreement on global warming. But hopes are slim that additional discussions will produce concrete plans to slash fossil fuel use. The added day of talks came as the two-week annual summit, or COP31 , drew strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels in a draft of the final agreement. The document is meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which drives heat waves, floods and other disasters. item.title: Trump downplays FBI data breach of NCIC, adds 'positive spin'
item.description: An FBI database that police all over the country use was hacked in the second major security breach in two months, and President Donald Trump downplayed it Saturday. The FBI's National Crime Information Center, which police use constantly, was hacked, CNN and NBC reported Friday night. The NCIC includes FBI fingerprint records, wanted persons, violent felons, missing persons and related information. Its use is restricted to law enforcement but is not classified. On Saturday, Trump said the breach is "not good," but that it could be helpful to him. We could "learn things that we would have never learned otherwise," he said. "I always like to put things in a positive spin," Trump said during a phone interview with Fox News when asked about the reports. "You had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. You had all of these other hoaxes. item.title: Russian cargo ship ablaze in Baltic Sea after drone strike, crew evacuates
item.description: HELSINKI — A Russian cargo ship with links to the military was hit by drones and caught fire in the Baltic Sea on Saturday in what Finland said was likely an attack by Ukraine, and the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters. The 16-member crew of the Sparta II evacuated onto lifeboats, then to a nearby Russian ship, and is on its way back to Russia, Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin told public broadcaster Yle late on Saturday. Ukraine has sent waves of military drones towards Russia's northwest Leningrad region this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of the Baltic region, leading to fears that the war was affecting NATO territory. "It is likely that Ukraine... is behind (the attack)," Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen told a press conference, adding it was not clear why the vessel had been targeted. The ship, bound for Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, Finland's Defense Forces said, corroborating an earlier account by Russian officials. item.title: Seoul district prepares to bring pet funerals directly to residents' doors
item.description: Courier scooters in Seoul deliver everything from midnight kimchi stew to designer handbags in under an hour, and soon grieving pet owners in the city's east will be able to summon a hearse just as easily. Starting in December, Seongdong District, located just east of downtown Seoul, will roll out a municipal mobile pet funeral service, dispatching specialized vans to residents' homes to collect deceased pets, hold a memorial ceremony and perform odorless, smoke-free cremations before returning the ashes in an urn. The initiative, finalized through a partnership signed earlier this month between the district office and local pet funeral operator Petmoon, tackles a thorny urban dilemma in Korea’s densely packed capital. While roughly 1 in 4 Korean households — an estimated 15 million people nationwide — now lives with a companion animal, strict zoning rules have pushed licensed pet crematoriums to the suburban fringes. For car-free Seoulites or elderly residents, saying a final goodbye often requires a lengthy, stressful trek out of the city. Under the new program, registered pet o

item.title: Herbalife Korea builds next chapter on 30 years of trust
item.description: Herbalife Korea’s next phase of growth will depend on lasting customer relationships rather than individual transactions, Herbalife Korea General Manager Sean Chung said, as the company marks its 30th anniversary in Korea by overhauling distributor compensation and introducing AI tools. The company’s history has been about helping Koreans build healthy nutrition habits, he said, arguing that sustainable growth comes from maintaining trust beyond a single sale. Since entering Korea in 1996, Herbalife has expanded from weight management products into everyday nutrition, protein, sports nutrition and beauty-related wellness as consumer priorities have evolved. Its first decade centered on its flagship Formula 1 shake brand, balancing nutrient intake and healthy eating habits in a market dominated by physical stores and face-to-face sales. From 2006 and 2015, the rapid growth of online shopping and hypermarkets intensified competition. During this period, Herbalife emphasized ongoing communication and communities that helped customers maintain habits they found difficult to sustain on t

item.title: Mountain festival brings foreign tourists to Seoul's peaks
item.description: In a sprawling metropolis better known globally for neon-lit shopping districts, K-pop studios and royal palaces, some of Seoul’s hottest tourist attractions this fall required sturdy boots and a willingness to work up a sweat. More than 13,000 hikers passed through Seoul’s mountain tourism centers during the three weeks of 2026 Seoul Hiking Week, which wrapped up Sunday, underscoring how Korea’s capital is successfully turning its rugged granite peaks into an urban playground. According to the Seoul Tourism Organization, which hosted the third edition of the autumn festival starting on Oct. 26, roughly 4,800 of the visitors to its three Seoul Hiking Tourism Centers were foreign nationals — a 48 percent jump from the same period in 2025. Seoul is built directly into a basin ringed by dozens of steep, forested peaks and ancient fortress walls. Trailheads sit steps from subway stations, allowing residents and tourists alike to step off a commuter train and start ascending mountain trails within minutes. item.title: More Chinese than Korean members: Why K-pop is becoming more multicultural
item.description: Six. That is the number of Chinese members in A2O Soul, the new group recently launched by producer Lee Soo-man's A2O Entertainment as he returns to Korea's K-pop market after a three-year hiatus. The multinational group consists of 15 members, with Chinese nationals accounting for 40 percent, the largest share of any nationality. Korean nationals, including those with dual citizenship, make up five members, or 33.3 percent. It is the first time a K-pop group debuting in Korea has more Chinese members than Korean ones. Multinational groups are nothing new in K-pop. However, among groups debuting in Korea, rather than overseas-localized acts, Korean members have traditionally made up the largest nationality group. Seventeen, for example, has two Chinese members, but 10 of its 13 members (76.9 percent) are Korean. Twice, which has three Japanese members, has five Koreans out of nine members (55.6 percent). Two groups that debuted in Korea, TimeZ in 2012 and UNIQ in 2014, also had more Chinese than Korean members. But their origins were different from those of A2O Soul. Both were joint Kore

item.title: Why are young Koreans falling for Japanese animated series 'Chiikawa?'
item.description: "I'm worried everything will sell out. They'll keep restocking, right?" A long line of customers stretched outside the Chiikawa Shop on the third floor of I'Park Mall in Yongsan District, Seoul, Nov. 5. A quick count put the number of people waiting at well over 50. They had come to buy merchandise featuring characters from the Japanese animated series "Chiikawa." One shopper, surnamed Kim, 27, emerged carrying a large bag filled with stuffed toys, figurines and key rings. "I came to love the animation because I find hope in the way Chiikawa overcomes life's hardships and grows along the way," Kim said with a laugh. "I kept adding things to my basket and ended up spending 460,000 won ($315)." "Chiikawa," created by Japanese manga artist Nagano, depicts the everyday lives of characters collectively described as "something small and cute." In Korea, the series has gained a large following not only among children but also among people in their 20s and 30s. The theatrical film "Chiikawa: The Secret of Mermaid Island," which opened Sept. 30, had attracted approximately 2.95 million moviegoer

item.title: Volcano Watch: Kilauea’s enigmatic past
item.description:
Kilauea recently underwent its 56th lava fountaining episode since December 2024. This is just the most-recent eruptive activity from one of the world’s most active volcanoes. While frequent eruptions add new land to Kilauea, lava flows and tephra deposits can also bury older erupted material. This can make it difficult to unravel the history of such an active volcano.

The post Volcano Watch: Kilauea’s enigmatic past appeared first on Hawaii Tribune-Herald.

item.title: Bus rams into pavement near Hongik University Station, injuring 6
item.description: A bus rammed into the pavement near Hongik University Station in Seoul on Saturday, injuring six people. The bus veered onto the pavement and crashed into a structure following a collision involving another bus and a sedan at around 6:57 p.m. in the busy entertainment district. Six people were taken to hospitals for treatment after sustaining injuries. No deaths or serious injuries have been reported. Police and fire authorities were looking into the exact cause of the accident.

item.title: BTS wins 5 MAMA awards as Cortis takes Song of the Year
item.description: K-pop supergroup BTS won five awards, including two grand prizes, at the 2026 MAMA Awards, which ran from Friday to Saturday, while rising boy group Cortis claimed Song of the Year, also a grand prize. On the second night of the ceremony Saturday at Kyocera Dome Osaka, BTS received Album of the Year for "Arirang" and Best Song Top 10 for "Swim," bringing its tally to five awards. The group won Artist of the Year, Best Male Group and a spot in the Fans' Choice Male Top 10 on the opening night. BTS, which did not attend the ceremony because of its world tour, delivered a video message. Member Suga said, "We're so grateful that our first album back as a group in such a long time has received so much love." Jungkook said the group returned to its fandom, ARMY, after three years and nine months wanting to show how much it had grown, adding that the members worked hard "to find honest stories that truly reflect who we are and what BTS stands for today." item.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits central Peru
item.description: LIMA — A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru's Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities. The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers. Peru's Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake "minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit." Belaunde added that there had been "no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health." AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake. The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao. Peru's National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to stro

item.title: FBI's criminal information database hacked, CNN reports
item.description: The FBI is investigating a suspected breach of a nationwide database used by federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information, CNN reported on Friday, citing two people briefed on the investigation. The apparent compromise of the National Crime Information Center database would mark the second intrusion involving an FBI system in recent months and the latest in a string of cyber incidents that have alarmed US officials over the past week. The agency did not respond to a request for comment from Reuters. The FBI database is used by law enforcement agencies nationwide to store and share information on warrants, criminal histories and background checks. Previous high-profile cyber disruptions over the past week have included a global outage affecting hundreds of millions of Microsoft users and a nationwide halt to air travel that disrupted more than 18,000 flights. A September breach by a digital extortion group known as "ShinyHunters" accessed an FBI jobs website, compromising data on current and former FBI employees.

item.title: Lee reiterates $75,000 reward for reporting cheating on CSAT
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung reiterated Saturday that the government will offer 100 million won ($75,000) in reward to anyone reporting those who cheated on this week's college entrance exam, calling the misconduct a "crime as serious as corruption" involving government officials. Lee made the comments on social media, saying the reward will be provided per case of cheating, meaning the total reward could be greater than 100 million won if one reports multiple cheating cases at once. Lee also said that if a cheater turns themselves in for their own cheating and reports other accomplices, they will receive a reduced punishment for their offense while still being paid the full reward for reporting. "Cheating on the college entrance exam is a crime as serious as corruption by public officials," Lee said. "We will track cheaters down to the very end and strictly punish exam cheating that steals the lifelong efforts of hundreds of thousands of test-takers." item.title: Jang Na-ra, Kim Hye-yoon spark fresh chemistry as 'Good Partner 2' premieres to strong ratings
item.description: SBS legal drama "Good Partner" has returned for its second season after nearly two years, introducing a new partnership between Jang Na-ra and Kim Hye-yoon that promises sharp courtroom confrontations, contrasting personalities and an evolving bond between two divorce lawyers. The first episode of "Good Partner 2," which aired Friday, recorded a nationwide viewership rating of 8.4 percent and a peak of 9.9 percent, according to Nielsen Korea. The figure surpassed the 7.8 percent premiere rating of the first season, giving the sequel a promising start. The new season follows Cha Eun-kyung (Jang), a seasoned divorce attorney who heads her own law firm, and Kang Hye-seong (Kim), a fiercely determined lawyer who joins her as a partner. The series is once again written by Choi Yu-na, a practicing divorce attorney who also penned the first season, while director Seo Min-jung takes the helm this time. Although divorce cases remain central to the story, the new season places greater emphasis on humor and warmth, using its colorful characters to balance the emotional weight of marital disputes. A
